value.title: Acura
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Acura ZDX (MY2025) ships with a CCS1 port and uses an Acura-approved CCS-to-NACS adapter (introduced June 2025) for Tesla Supercharger access — over 23,500 selected Superchargers in the US. ZDX owners also get bundled access to Electrify America and EVgo via Honda/Acura agreements announced in 2023. The MY2026 RSX will ship with a native NACS port (Acura's first), with CCS adapter for legacy networks. Sources: https://acuranews.com/en-US/releases/release-ccb19723f8c4bc9d353bc56a2c0ee138-acura-zdx-owners-now-have-access-to-tesla-supercharger-network-with-approved-adapters , https://acuranews.com/en-US/releases/release-cc39196e84787a20ec3cb086fb215129-honda-and-acura-electric-vehicles-will-have-access-to-largest-ev-charging-networks-in-north-america-aided-by-new-agreements-with-evgo-and-electrify-america
value.drmPolicy: Acura uses AcuraLink connected services with subscription tiers (Standard, Security, Premium). The Standard package includes automatic collision notification and emergency calling. Higher tiers (Security, Premium) unlock remote start, vehicle finder, geofencing, speed alerts, and concierge — typically free for a trial period (3-12 months on new vehicles) then $14.99-$24.99/month. Core driving functions, infotainment, wireless CarPlay/Android Auto do not require subscription. The 2026 RSX will introduce Honda's new ASIMO operating system with OTA updates and driver-behavior learning, which may shift more features behind connectivity. No documented post-sale remote feature reductions for the Acura brand as of 2026-05. Sources: https://www.acura.com/owners/acuralink , https://www.cars.com/articles/hybrids-evs-and-performance-honda-acura-have-big-plans-for-the-next-few-years-520305/
value.electrificationStrategy: Acura's electrification strategy emphasizes a multi-pillar approach: gas-powered performance (Integra, TLX, ADX), hybrid efficiency (next-gen RDX/MDX in development), and full-electric (ZDX, RSX). The ZDX (MY2025), built on GM's Ultium platform, served as a bridge BEV but was discontinued in September 2025 after only 18 months of production due to low sales. The 2026 RSX is Acura's first in-house EV, built on Honda's global EV platform at the new EV Hub in Ohio, with NACS port standard. Parent Honda plans 15 new Honda/Acura hybrid models globally (primarily North America) by 2030, and Acura has stated future Acura performance cars will all be hybrid. Source: https://acuranews.com/en-US/releases/next-generation-acura-rdx-will-go-hybrid , https://www.cars.com/articles/hybrids-evs-and-performance-honda-acura-have-big-plans-for-the-next-few-years-520305/
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: Acura has not made public statements specifically addressing the IIJA Section 24220 impaired-driving-detection mandate (expected ~2027). As a Honda subsidiary, Acura is expected to follow Honda's compliance approach. NHTSA has not finalized the rule as of 2026-05, and Honda/Acura have generally adopted Sensing/AcuraWatch driver-monitoring systems that include camera-based attention monitoring (face/eye tracking) on newer models (e.g., MDX Type S, ZDX), which could form the substrate for passive impairment detection. No public hardware vs software disclosure. Source attempted: NHTSA press releases, acuranews.com, no Acura-specific position found.
value.reliabilityNotes: Acura is consistently a top-tier reliability brand. Consumer Reports placed Acura around 5th in its 2024-2025 brand reliability rankings. J.D. Power 2025 ratings: MDX scores 83/100 (Great), RDX scores 81/100 (Great); Acura RDX ranked highest in the Compact Premium SUV segment in J.D. Power's 2025 Initial Quality Study (IQS). RepairPal gives Acura 4.0/5.0 (2nd out of 32 brands). The ZDX is a new BEV (built on GM's Ultium platform), so brand-level Acura reliability does not necessarily extend — early Ultium platform issues (Cadillac LYRIQ, Honda Prologue) may apply. Sources: https://www.jdpower.com/cars/2025/acura/mdx , https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/acura/ , https://www.jalopnik.com/1977147/acura-reliability-consumer-reports/

value.title: Aston Martin
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Aston Martin has not announced an NACS / Tesla Supercharger partnership. The Valhalla (the only electrified Aston Martin in MY2025/2026) is a PHEV with ~9 mi EV range and a small 6.1 kWh battery; charging-network access is not a marketed feature. No bundled free-charging promotion identified. Future BEV (~2030) charging-port strategy unannounced; Aston Martin's technical partnership with Lucid (NACS-aligned) is suggestive but not confirmed. Sources: https://windingroad.com/articles/features/automakers-embrace-tesla-nacs-proprietary-supercharger-network/ ; https://www.astonmartin.com/en-us/models/valhalla
value.drmPolicy: Aston Martin Connected Car Services (telematics, remote lock/unlock, vehicle location, OTA, app) are provided complimentary for the first 3 years from warranty start. After that, owners must subscribe to retain Connected services; pricing is set 'at the prevailing annual rate' and not publicly disclosed. App functionality requires a paid 'Convenience', 'Advantage', 'Vehicle Maintenance', 'Vehicle Service', or 'Support Services' package. Core driving functions are not known to be subscription-locked, but remote/app features lapse without renewal. No public reports of Aston Martin remotely disabling propulsion or features post-sale. Sources: https://www.astonmartin.com/en-us/legal/am-connected-car-system-terms-and-conditions ; https://www.astonmartin.com/en-us/legal/aston-martin-connected-car-system-privacy-policy
value.electrificationStrategy: Aston Martin has delayed its first BEV from 2026 to the end of the decade (now targeted around 2030). The current strategy emphasizes plug-in hybrid (PHEV) and mild-hybrid (MHEV) derivatives. The Valhalla (launched as a 2026 model) is the brand's first PHEV. A BEV is planned for around 2030, joined by another PHEV the same year, with hybrid derivatives continuing through 2035. Sources: https://www.wardsauto.com/news/aston-martin-delays-bev-model-targeting-more-hybrids-and-keeping-v-12/778352/ ; https://www.electrive.com/2022/02/03/aston-martin-to-focus-on-hybrid-and-electric-cars-from-2026/
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: No public statement from Aston Martin specific to the federal IIJA impaired-driving-detection mandate (NHTSA Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking) was found in searches of news, regulatory filings, and forums as of 2026-05. As a low-volume luxury OEM (~6,000 units/yr globally), Aston Martin is expected to follow the Alliance for Automotive Innovation industry position (which argues more research is needed before mandate) and implement whatever NHTSA finalizes via passive driver-monitoring camera/biometric sensing already present in DB12/Vantage/DBX driver-attention systems. value.title: Audi
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Audi's primary US charging partnership remains Electrify America (VW Group's settlement-funded network, ~5,000 DC fast chargers). Audi e-tron purchasers historically received complimentary EA charging credits at purchase. Beginning September 9, 2025, Audi added access to ~23,500 Tesla NACS Superchargers via a UL2252-certified Audi NACS DC Charging Adapter, which is included as a port-installed accessory on new Q6 e-tron, A6 Sportback e-tron, and e-tron GT models from 2025 MY forward. The Q4 e-tron is explicitly excluded from approved NACS adapter use, and the adapter is DC-only (not for AC L1/L2 or Tesla Destination Chargers). Sessions are paid through the Tesla app, not Audi's. Combined access: ~28,000 DCFC stations. Sources: https://media.audiusa.com/releases/643 ; https://www.audiusa.com/en/ev-hub/layer/nacs-faqs/ ; https://www.electrive.com/2025/09/08/audi-and-porsche-ev-drivers-gain-nacs-adapters/
value.drmPolicy: Audi vehicles use the myAudi connected-services platform (Audi connect) plus the MMI infotainment system. Connectivity is required for the full myAudi feature set (remote lock/unlock, remote start, stolen-vehicle locator, geofencing/curfew/valet/speed alerts, OTA updates) but the car itself drives normally without an active subscription. After an initial complimentary period, Audi connect services move to paid subscription. Audi has been an early adopter of 'Function on Demand' subscription features: customers can activate options post-purchase via the myAudi app on a monthly, annual, or lifetime basis (e.g., MMI Navigation plus on equipped hardware, adaptive cruise upgrades, high-beam assist). In Canada the MMI Navigation FoD has been advertised at roughly CA$64.90/month or CA$649.25/year. Audi has not been publicly documented as remotely disabling already-purchased features post-sale. Sources: https://www.audiusa.com/en/inside-audi/innovation/audi-connect/audi-connect-function-on-demand/ ; https://www.topspeed.com/audi-subscription-based-services/ ; https://carbuzz.com/news/audi-joins-the-subscription-game-with-function-on-demand/ ; https://www.autoevolution.com/news/audi-joins-the-subscription-bandwagon-with-8499-monthly-fee-for-mmi-navigation-161434.html
value.electrificationStrategy: Audi has walked back its previous commitment to launch its final new ICE model by 2026 and phase out combustion engines by 2033. In mid-2025, CEO Gernot Doellner confirmed Audi has scrapped any fixed ICE phase-out deadline, citing slower-than-expected global EV adoption, and committed to a flexible multi-powertrain strategy (BEV + PHEV + ICE) for at least another 7-10 years. Audi will launch a completely new wave of petrol and plug-in hybrid vehicles between 2024 and 2026 alongside the e-tron / e-hybrid lineup. The corporate carbon-neutrality target of 2050 remains. Sources: https://www.electrive.com/2025/06/19/audi-scraps-ice-phase-out-deadline/ ; https://insideevs.com/news/726706/audi-electric-2026-plan/ ; https://www.cartoq.com/car-news/audi-abandons-2033-all-electric-deadline-revives-ice-development/
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: Audi has made no public US-specific statement about the IIJA-driven federal impaired-driving-detection mandate (NHTSA Advanced Impaired Driving Prevention Technology rulemaking, expected ~2027). As a VW Group brand, Audi will inherit whatever group-level implementation is adopted. Group-wide there is no published Audi-branded position on hardware vs software approach, bypassability, or driver-opt-out. Searches across Audi MediaCenter, Audi USA, and trade press returned no Audi statement on the NHTSA Notice of Proposed Rulemaking. Expect compliance to follow whatever VW Group standardizes — likely a software/driver-monitoring camera approach building on existing attention-assist hardware in MQB-evo / PPC / PPE platforms.
value.reliabilityNotes: Audi finished last (32nd) in the J.D. Power 2025 U.S. Initial Quality Study with 269 PP100, up from 242 PP100 in 2024 — meaning more reported problems, not fewer. Consumer Reports ranks Audi 7th overall in brand reliability for 2025, below average for predicted reliability, with infotainment glitches and oil leaks the most cited issues. Q5 and A4 rate as the brand's more reliable nameplates; EVs (e-tron / Q4 e-tron) have a shorter track record and a history of recalls (notably the discontinued e-tron / e-tron Sportback brake-pedal-detachment recall). value.title: Bentley
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Bentley does not have a public NACS adoption announcement as of May 2026; PHEVs in the lineup use the J1772 (Type 1) port for AC L2 home/public charging and do not DC fast-charge (peak ~11 kW AC). No bundled charging-network partnership equivalent to Mercedes-Benz/Electrify America or Ford/Tesla. Buyers can use any J1772 EVgo/ChargePoint/EA L2 station; the 25.9 kWh Continental/Flying Spur PHEV battery and 18 kWh Bentayga Hybrid battery do not require DC fast charging. Sources: https://www.bentleymotors.com/en/models/continental-gt/continental-gt-speed.html
value.drmPolicy: Bentley vehicles use the 'My Bentley' connected services platform for OTA updates, remote functions, concierge, and navigation/traffic data, broadly comparable to Audi/Porsche connect (shared VW Group MIB infotainment stack). The car operates fully without connectivity for core driving functions, but connected features (remote lock/unlock, find-my-car, live traffic, OTA map updates) require an active My Bentley subscription after the initial complimentary period. No publicly documented cases of Bentley remotely disabling post-sale features. The Continental GT/GTC and Flying Spur PHEVs share the Porsche Panamera E-Hybrid drivetrain electronics, which run a Porsche-style modular OTA system. Sources: https://support.bentleymotors.com/eu/en/support-bentley.html
value.electrificationStrategy: Bentley's revised Beyond100+ strategy (announced Nov 2024) pushes the all-electric-only target from 2030 to 2035. The plan calls for a new PHEV or BEV model every year of the next decade, with PHEV lifecycles extended beyond 2030. The first Bentley BEV — a 'Luxury Urban SUV' positioned below the Bentayga — is slated to debut in 2026. As of MY2025 the Continental GT, Continental GTC, and Flying Spur lineups are 100% PHEV (V8 + electric); the Bentayga is sold as either a V6 PHEV ('Hybrid') or a V8 (ICE). Sources: https://www.bentleymedia.com/en/newsitem/1648 ; https://theevreport.com/bentley-extends-beyond100-strategy-to-2035 ; https://www.bentleymotors.com/en/about-bentley/beyond-100/coming-this-way.html
value.killSwitchPolicy: No Bentley-specific public statement on the IIJA-driven federal impaired-driving-detection mandate (NHTSA missed its 2024 deadline; rulemaking remains open as of 2026). Bentley vehicles inherit the VW Group driver-monitoring camera system used in newer Audi/Porsche/VW models (camera-based attention monitoring), which is a likely substrate for any future impairment-detection compliance, but Bentley has not committed publicly to a hardware vs. software approach. Sources: https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/ ; https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/1137
value.reliabilityNotes: Bentley is not separately ranked in J.D. Power's 2025 Vehicle Dependability Study (too-low-volume brand). Consumer Reports does not publish full Bentley reliability scores either. Anecdotal industry consensus (Edmunds, MotorTrend, owner forums): post-Bentayga-generation Bentleys (2016+) are materially more reliable than the W12-era cars but still trail mainstream luxury (Lexus, Porsche) on long-term cost; common complaints involve infotainment quirks, air-suspension component costs, and PHEV-era electronics. NHTSA recall 2025-2026: high-pressure fuel pump bolt joint on V8 Evo engine (affects Continental GT/GTC and 2025 Flying Spur), 17 units, fire-risk. value.title: BMW
value.chargingNetworkAccess:
BMW EVs in the US gained access to the Tesla Supercharger network in December 2025 via a BMW-certified CCS-to-NACS adapter; official adapters go on sale Q2 2026. Existing 2025/2026 BMW EVs (i4, i5, i7, iX) use CCS1 native ports plus the adapter; Neue Klasse models (iX3, i3 sedan, 2025 onward) will ship with NACS ports natively. BMW EVs receive 3 years of complimentary 30-minute charging sessions at Electrify America stations; additional networks reachable via the My BMW app include EVgo and ChargePoint. BMW is a founding partner in IONNA, the seven-OEM joint venture building a new 30,000+ stall North American high-power charging network slated to begin operations in 2025-2026.

Sources:
- https://electrek.co/2025/12/10/bmw-evs-access-tesla-supercharger-network-today/
- https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/usa/article/detail/T0437767EN_US/
- https://www.bmwusa.com/explore/electric/charging.html
value.drmPolicy:
BMW operates the ConnectedDrive platform and Functions on Demand (post-purchase software upgrades). In 2022 BMW began charging subscriptions in select markets (UK, Germany, South Korea) for heated seats already physically present in cars, generating major consumer backlash; the company discontinued the heated-seat subscription in late 2023 but continues to offer post-purchase software upgrades (high-beam assist, adaptive cruise, driving-assistant features) through ConnectedDrive. BMW has stated it remains committed to a features-as-a-service model. iDrive infotainment requires periodic OTA updates; vehicles can operate locally but lose remote features (My BMW app, charging coordination, traffic, eCall) without connectivity.

Sources:
- https://www.thedrive.com/news/bmw-commits-to-subscriptions-even-after-heated-seat-debacle
- https://www.techspot.com/news/111208-bmw-admits-heated-seat-subscriptions-mistake-but-commits.html
- https://consumerrights.wiki/w/BMW%27s_heated_seat_subscription
value.electrificationStrategy:
BMW Group targets BEVs to comprise at least 50% of global sales by 2030, with no fixed phase-out date for ICE. The Neue Klasse platform launches in 2025-2026 as the foundation for next-generation BMW EVs, beginning with the iX3 (2025) and i3 sedan (2026). BMW pursues a multi-powertrain strategy (BEV, PHEV, ICE, FCEV) rather than an all-electric mandate, and dropped its prior 'Power of Choice' deadline goals in favor of customer-led adoption pacing.

Sources:
- https://www.bmwgroup.com/en/news/general/2023/neue-klasse.html
- https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/global/article/detail/T0438211EN/bmw-group-strategy-update
value.killSwitchPolicy:
BMW has not publicly committed to a specific hardware vs software architecture for the IIJA-mandated impaired-driving-detection system. BMW (along with Ford, GM, Toyota) wrote to NHTSA in 2024 stating general support for the initiative but raising concerns about consumer acceptance and accuracy. As of May 2026, NHTSA has reported that no technology meets the required accuracy threshold and the 2027 deadline appears unlikely to be met. Current BMW vehicles already include in-cabin Driver Attention Camera (in some markets / on certain trims with Driving Assistant Professional / Highway Assistant) used for hands-off attention monitoring; this hardware could plausibly be repurposed for impairment detection but BMW has made no public statement to that effect.

Sources:

- https://advocacy.consumerreports.org/research/technical-working-group-on-advanced-impaired-driving-prevention-technology-views-statement-on-implementing-driver-impairment-prevention-technology/
value.reliabilityNotes:
Consumer Reports 2025 brand rankings placed BMW #2 overall (behind Subaru), above Porsche, Lexus, Honda, Toyota. JD Power 2025 Initial Quality Study reported 196 problems per 100 BMWs (industry average: 192), placing BMW slightly below average but improved from 206 PP100 in 2024. BMW X7 won its Large Premium SUV segment; X6 won Upper Midsize Premium SUV. Reliability concerns historically center on complex electronics (iDrive, ConnectedDrive), oil consumption on N-series engines, and high out-of-warranty repair costs. BEV reliability data is still limited; iX has had software-related recalls but generally tracks the brand average.

value.title: Bugatti
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Bugatti has announced no partnership with Tesla Supercharger, Electrify America, EVgo, or ChargePoint networks. The Tourbillon's 25 kWh PHEV battery is sized for ~37 mi (60 km) of EV-only driving and is expected to be home-charged via the customer's private infrastructure; Bugatti has not published DC fast-charge specs or a public network strategy. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bugatti_Tourbillon
value.drmPolicy: Bugatti publicly describes a 'Connected Car' telemetry layer used during development and for in-life diagnostics: vehicles transmit operating data (engine, transmission, chassis) to Molsheim for prognostics and maintenance scheduling. There is no public evidence Bugatti has remotely disabled features post-sale, gated horsepower behind a subscription, or required permanent internet for core driving operation. Software updates are delivered through authorized service centers rather than mass-market over-the-air consumer pushes. Given the bespoke ultra-low-volume customer relationship (sub-300 unit production runs), the brand has not been implicated in the subscription-feature controversies seen at BMW/Mercedes. Source: https://newsroom.bugatti.com/en/press-releases/connected-car-la-bugatti
value.electrificationStrategy: Bugatti's electrification strategy is defined by the Bugatti Rimac joint venture (formed 2021) under CEO Mate Rimac. The brand has transitioned from the pure-ICE quad-turbo W16 era (Chiron, Mistral) to a plug-in hybrid V16 era beginning with the Tourbillon (1,800 hp, 25 kWh, 800V; deliveries 2026). Rimac Technology supplies the high-voltage battery, electric motors, and inverter. Bugatti has not announced a fully battery-electric model or a hard date for going all-electric; the stated direction is hybrid hypercars that preserve naturally aspirated combustion character while adding EV instant torque. Source: https://www.rimac-newsroom.com/press-releases/rimac-technology/rimac-technology-powers-the-bugatti-tourbillon-with-cutting-edge-battery-and-powe ; https://newsroom.bugatti.com/en/press-releases/the-bugatti-tourbillon-an-automotive-icon-pour-leternite
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: Bugatti has made no public statement on the IIJA Section 24220 impaired-driving-detection mandate. NHTSA missed its November 2024 deadline and as of early 2026 has reported that available technologies do not meet required accuracy levels, so no manufacturer-specific compliance plans are public. Sources searched: NHTSA rulemaking trackers, Bugatti newsroom, dallasexpress and autoguide reporting on the IIJA timeline. TrueDelta does not aggregate Bugatti reliability data. Anecdotal owner reports for the Veyron/Chiron era describe high service costs and long lead times for replacement parts but few catastrophic failures; the Tourbillon as a new V16 + Rimac hybrid platform has no field reliability history as of 2026-05-21.

value.title: Buick
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Buick currently has no plug-in vehicles in the US, so charging-network access is theoretical pending the brand's delayed EV launch. GM-wide announcements that would inherit to Buick include: (1) NACS adoption via the Tesla Supercharger network beginning in 2024 for GM brands via CCS-to-NACS adapter, transitioning to native NACS ports starting in MY2025 vehicles ([gmauthority.com — GM NACS](https://gmauthority.com/blog/2023/06/general-motors-confirms-it-will-adopt-tesla-nacs-charging-standard-starting-in-2025/)). (2) GM's Ultium Charge 360 partnership network aggregating EVgo, ChargePoint, Blink, Flo, and Shell Recharge with one-app payment integration via the myBuick app ([gm.com — Ultium Charge 360](https://www.gm.com/electric-vehicles/charging)). (3) EVgo partnership to deploy 3,250+ DC fast-charging stalls. None of this is actually consumable by US Buick buyers today because the brand sells no plug-in vehicles in the US for MY2025 or MY2026.
value.drmPolicy: Buick vehicles use GM's standard OnStar / Buick Connected Services telematics platform shared across all GM brands. Cars can be driven offline (no subscription required for basic operation), but Connected Services features (remote start via app, remote door lock, vehicle locator, in-vehicle Wi-Fi hotspot, navigation, and over-the-air updates) require active OnStar/Connected Services subscriptions after the initial trial period. GM has been at the center of consumer-data-sale controversies: in 2024, the FTC found that GM (including Buick) had been selling granular driving telematics data (hard-braking, hard-acceleration, speeding events) to data brokers LexisNexis and Verisk via the OnStar Smart Driver program, who then sold scores to auto insurers, resulting in surprise rate hikes for consumers ([nytimes.com — GM Settles FTC](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/01/16/business/general-motors-onstar-ftc-settlement.html)). GM agreed in January 2025 to a 5-year FTC consent order banning sale of geolocation/driver-behavior data to consumer-reporting agencies. GM also operates over-the-air (OTA) software updates on most 2020+ Buicks via the Vehicle Intelligence Platform, including the ability to deliver, gate, or modify features remotely. Subscription-gated features have included Super Cruise (hands-free highway driving, subscription required after 3-year trial — though Super Cruise is not offered on any current US Buick).
value.electrificationStrategy: Buick has publicly committed to going "all-electric by 2030" in North America, announced alongside the unveiling of the Wildcat EV concept and a new badge identity in 2022 ([buick.com Electric Vehicle Future](https://www.buick.com/explore/news/electric-vehicle-future)). However, the US lineup remains entirely ICE-only through MY2026: every 2025 and 2026 US Buick (Envista, Encore GX, Envision, Enclave) uses a turbocharged gasoline engine with no hybrid or BEV variant ([fourwheelask.com](https://fourwheelask.com/does-buick-have-a-hybrid-suv/), [carbuzz.com 2026 Buick SUVs](https://carbuzz.com/2026-buick-suvs-ranked-by-price/)). Buick's first US EV (the China-built Electra E5) was deferred from 2024 to 2025, then delayed indefinitely in mid-2024 citing tariffs on Chinese-built EVs ([gmauthority.com — Electra E5 Delayed](https://gmauthority.com/blog/2024/07/buick-electra-e5-delayed-indefinitely-in-the-u-s/), [autoblog.com](https://www.autoblog.com/features/buick-ev-delayed-for-the-u-s-market-new-timeline-uncertain)). New 2026 Electra-badge vehicles (E7 PHEV, L7 EREV sedan) are confirmed China-only ([electrek.co](https://electrek.co/2025/10/02/2026-buick-electra-erev-arrives-190-miles-of-ev-range-and-an-affordable-price/), [gmauthority.com Electra E7 PHEV](https://gmauthority.com/blog/2026/01/brand-new-2026-buick-electra-e7-phev-first-official-images/)). The "all-electric by 2030" goal therefore appears aspirational rather than executable on its original timeline given Buick's current zero-electrified US lineup with no domestically-built EV announced.
value.killSwitchPolicy: Buick has not made a brand-specific public statement on the IIJA-mandated impaired-driving detection requirement (NHTSA's pending Advanced Impaired Driving Prevention Technology rulemaking under Section 24220 of the 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, originally targeted for ~2027 model-year deployment but currently in extended rulemaking with no final rule as of 2026). As a GM brand, Buick will inherit whatever fleet-wide approach GM adopts. GM has not publicly committed to a specific implementation; the Alliance for Automotive Innovation (the trade group representing GM and most major OEMs) has lobbied for a passive, sensor-based approach (driver-monitoring cameras + steering-input analysis) rather than alcohol-specific interlocks, and has argued for delayed implementation citing technology-readiness concerns ([autoinnovators.org statements on Section 24220](https://www.autosinnovate.org/issues/policy/road-safety)). All current Buicks ship with GM's Driver Attention Assist (eye-tracking camera in the steering wheel, currently only used to issue alerts and to gate Super Cruise hands-free operation on cars equipped with it). The hardware foundation for camera-based driver-state monitoring is therefore already deployed across the Buick lineup and could be repurposed for an impairment-detection mandate via OTA software update, though Buick has not confirmed this. No bypass mechanism has been announced. Data unavailable: any Buick-specific public statement on impaired-driving detection — the company has been silent and defers to GM and the Alliance for Automotive Innovation.
value.reliabilityNotes: Buick has consistently ranked above industry average in JD Power's Initial Quality Study and Vehicle Dependability Study over the past several years, often appearing in the top 5–10 brands and at times leading non-luxury brand reliability rankings. JD Power's 2024 US Vehicle Dependability Study ranked Buick at 158 problems per 100 vehicles, better than the industry average of 190 ([jdpower.com — 2024 VDS](https://www.jdpower.com/business/press-releases/2024-us-vehicle-dependability-study-vds)). Consumer Reports' 2024 annual reliability brand rankings placed Buick mid-pack among 30 brands, with the Encore GX rated average and the Envision rated above average for predicted reliability ([consumerreports.org car-brand reliability](https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/car-reliability-owner-satisfaction/who-makes-the-most-reliable-cars-a7824554938/)). TrueDelta tracks the Encore GX (introduced 2020) and Envision (2nd-gen 2021+) with generally average repair-frequency curves; the Envista (introduced 2024) has too little data for a stable signal as of mid-2026 ([truedelta.com Buick](https://www.truedelta.com/Buick/reliability)). Major known issues are tied to shared GM components: the 9-speed automatic in Envision/Enclave has had reported harsh-shifting complaints, and the 1.2L/1.3L turbo three-cylinder engines in Envista/Encore GX have generated some early-life concerns about long-term durability of the small displacement turbo platform under sustained high-load use.

value.title: Cadillac
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Cadillac EVs use the CCS1 connector through MY2025; MY2026 begins the native NACS transition, starting with the 2026 Optiq, which is Cadillac's first model to natively feature the Tesla NACS port. All current Cadillac EVs (Lyriq, Optiq, Lyriq-V, Vistiq, Escalade IQ/IQL) are Tesla Supercharger-compatible when equipped with the approved NACS adapter, available for $225 through the Cadillac mobile app. Cadillac participates in GM's broader charging network access, which includes EVgo, ChargePoint, Blink, and Flo via the myCadillac app. Optiq purchasers have received a complimentary home Level 2 charger installation offer and public charging credits in past promotions. Sources: [Tustin Cadillac](https://www.tustincadillac.com/which-cadillac-evs-can-use-tesla-superchargers/), [Cadillac Pasadena](https://www.cadillacpasadena.com/cadillac-research/cadillacs-tesla-superchargers/), [Cadillac Laval](https://cadillaclaval.com/en/the-2026-cadillac-optiq-nacs).
value.drmPolicy: All current Cadillac EVs ship with OnStar/Cadillac Connected Services. MY2025+ vehicles receive 8 years of core OnStar features (automatic crash response, remote commands, voice assistant, navigation) included. Subscription tiers gate additional features: Connect plan ($9.99/mo for MY2025+), Connect Plus ($24.99/mo for Wi-Fi hotspot, video streaming, browser), Protect ($19.99/mo for MY2025+ — roadside, safety, stolen vehicle assist, Guardian app), and OnStar One ($49.99/mo bundle excluding Super Cruise). Super Cruise is sold as a separate subscription after the included trial. GM CEO Mary Barra has publicly stated GM wants "even greater revenue" from OnStar and Super Cruise subscriptions, signaling continued growth in subscription-gated features. Vehicles include a 1-month OnStar One trial, plus 2 additional months if you subscribe within the trial. Sources: [OnStar Pricing](https://www.onstar.com/pricing), [CarBuzz on GM Subscription Strategy](https://carbuzz.com/gm-more-subscription-services/), [Cadillac OnStar](https://www.cadillac.com/technology/onstar).
value.electrificationStrategy: Cadillac originally announced an all-electric lineup by 2030, but in May 2024 Global VP John Roth walked that back, stating EVs and ICE will coexist for a number of years. The brand is not cutting EV programs and continues its step-ladder EV strategy: Optiq (entry), Lyriq (midsize), Vistiq (3-row), Escalade IQ (full-size), and the bespoke Celestiq grand tourer. As of MY2026, Cadillac sells no PHEVs or HEVs in the US — its electrified lineup is BEV-only. Sources: [GMAuthority May 2024](https://gmauthority.com/blog/2024/05/cadillac-changes-course-on-all-electric-by-2030-plan/), [Electrek May 2024](https://electrek.co/2024/05/02/cadillac-balks-plans-all-e-2030-may-still-offer-gas-cars-number-of-years/), [Cadillac Society](https://cadillacsociety.com/2024/05/02/cadillac-walks-back-its-plan-to-go-all-electric-2030-plan/).
value.killSwitchPolicy: Cadillac has not publicly outlined a specific implementation for the IIJA Section 24220 impaired-driving-detection mandate. GM (Cadillac's parent) has reportedly developed cameras and sensors that analyze a person walking to the driver's side door to detect potential impairment, but this is exploratory. NHTSA has missed its 2024 rulemaking deadline and has stated that no commercially available technology yet detects driver alcohol impairment accurately and passively. The mandate is expected to take effect for MY2027 or later. Existing Cadillac EVs already have driver-monitoring cameras (used for Super Cruise hands-free operation), which positions GM/Cadillac to repurpose camera-based monitoring for impairment detection. Sources: [The Autopian on IIJA Section 24220](https://www.theautopian.com/new-cars-sold-in-america-will-be-actively-watching-and-judging-you-and-may-decide-to-not-let-you-drive/), [KBB on the mandate](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/).
value.reliabilityNotes: Mixed signals. Consumer Reports' December 2025 New Car Reliability Report ranks Cadillac low — both the Lyriq and the newer Optiq earn below-average or well-below-average reliability marks, with issues concentrated in software, electronics, charging, and build quality. The 2025 Lyriq has been recalled 3 times by NHTSA. The Ultium battery architecture itself has not shown widespread degradation issues. GM has its own GM Energy charging network and partners with EVgo, ChargePoint, Blink, FLO, and Electrify America via the Plug & Charge / Plug and Charge-compatible flow. New Chevrolet EVs include limited public-charging credits at purchase (varies by program). value.drmPolicy: Chevrolet EVs are tightly integrated with OnStar connected services. Most connectivity features require an OnStar subscription after the included trial; Super Cruise (hands-free ADAS) requires an active OnStar Super Cruise plan (~$25-65/month depending on tier) to continue functioning after the included 3-year trial. The core vehicle drives without connectivity, but features such as remote start, navigation, OTA updates, in-vehicle apps, and Super Cruise degrade or stop once the subscription lapses. GM has not historically remotely disabled driving features post-sale on Chevrolet EVs, but the Blazer EV had a notable manufacturer-initiated stop-sale and software remediation in late 2023 / early 2024 after widespread software bugs, demonstrating GM's ability to halt and update fleet behavior via OTA. GM also drew significant criticism in 2024 for sharing Chevrolet driving telemetry with data brokers (LexisNexis, Verisk) without clear consent, leading to an FTC settlement banning such sharing for five years. Sources: [FTC v. GM 2025 settlement](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/01/ftc-takes-action-against-general-motors-sharing-drivers-precise-location-driving-behavior-data), [Blazer EV stop-sale](https://www.theverge.com/2023/12/20/24010098/gm-chevy-blazer-ev-stop-sale-software-issues), [OnStar Super Cruise plan](https://www.onstar.com/services/super-cruise).

GM has since softened the timeline by re-introducing plug-in hybrids in 2027 and slowing some BEV factory ramps, but Chevrolet continues to expand its EV lineup with the Equinox EV, Blazer EV, Silverado EV, and the returning Bolt (MY2027). Sources: [GM 2021 announcement](https://www.gm.com/commitments/zero-emissions), [Reuters on PHEV pivot](https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/gm-says-it-will-add-plug-in-hybrid-models-north-america-2023-01-31/), [GM news on 2027 Bolt](https://news.gm.com/home.detail.html/Pages/news/us/en/2025/oct/1009-2027-Chevrolet-Bolt.html).
value.killSwitchPolicy: GM has not publicly committed to a specific implementation for the IIJA Section 24220 impaired-driving-detection mandate. GM already offers OnStar Stolen Vehicle Slowdown, which lets law enforcement, via GM personnel, slow or stop a stolen vehicle - this is an opt-in OnStar feature, not the impaired-driver mandate. GM has filed comments in NHTSA's ANPRM process. The NHTSA final rule has not yet been issued (as of May 2026), so the implementation - camera-based behavioral, breath sensor, touch sensor - is not yet defined for Chevrolet. Existing Chevrolet EVs already ship driver-attention cameras for Super Cruise, so a camera-based behavioral implementation is the most plausible path. Sources: [NHTSA ANPRM RIN 2127-AM50](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/01/05/2023-28412/advanced-impaired-driving-prevention-technology), [OnStar Stolen Vehicle Slowdown](https://www.onstar.com/services/safety-security).

value.chargingNetworkAccess: Stellantis announced in late 2025 / early 2026 that its BEVs would gain Tesla Supercharger access via a $250 CCS1-to-NACS adapter starting in 2026 in North America. The agreement covers post-2024 model years of Dodge Charger Daytona, Jeep Wagoneer S/Recon, Ram ProMaster EV, Fiat 500e, and Maserati Folgore models. Chrysler has no BEV in production today, so the access is forward-looking. Local in-vehicle features (drive, climate, radio without satellite) continue to work without a subscription. Owner reports on Pacifica forums confirm that letting Connected Services lapse disables remote start, door lock/unlock, and tire-pressure viewing in the Chrysler app until re-enrolled. The vehicle itself does not require an active subscription or internet connectivity to drive. Over-the-air updates are pushed via Uconnect for infotainment and some vehicle-system software. value.title: Ford
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Ford was the first non-Tesla automaker to gain US/Canada Tesla Supercharger access (Feb 2024) for retail F-150 Lightning and Mustang Mach-E owners via a CCS1-to-NACS adapter. Initial Ford-issued adapters were free Feb 29 - Jun 30 2024; after that the Ford-Lectron adapter is $200. Some early adapters were recalled for port damage. Ford planned to ship NACS-native ports from 2025, but as of MY2025/2026 Mach-E and Lightning both ship with native CCS1 + included/optional NACS adapter — built-in NACS port adoption has slipped. BlueOval Charge Network aggregates ~150,000+ public chargers (Electrify America, EVgo, ChargePoint, Tesla Supercharger). Earlier complimentary EA charging promos for Mach-E (250 kWh complimentary on certain MY2023+ purchases) have largely wound down. Sources: [Electrek on Supercharger launch](https://electrek.co/2024/02/29/ford-tesla-supercharger-adapter-now-available/), [Lectron adapter](https://ev-lectron.com/blogs/news/ford-launches-new-nacs-adapter-in-partnership-with-lectron), [Consumer Reports on EV Supercharger access](https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/hybrids-evs/tesla-superchargers-open-to-other-evs-what-to-know-a9262067544/).
value.drmPolicy: Ford uses FordPass connectivity for remote start, vehicle status, and OTA updates; the vehicle itself runs core functions offline but many connected features (remote start, location, FordPass Rewards, FordPass Charging) require an active modem and the FordPass app. BlueCruise hands-free driving is sold as a subscription: $495/year, $49.99/month, or a $2,495 one-time prepay covering ~7 years (Oct 2024 pricing). Trial: 90 days complimentary. If subscription lapses the hands-free function disables but lane-keep/adaptive cruise (Co-Pilot360 ACC) remain. Ford has used OTA delivery to enable, change, and restrict features — most prominently the BlueCruise 1.2/1.3 lane-change behaviors and the on/off-ramp Hands-Free Lane Change rollout. Multiple NHTSA BlueCruise investigations are open as of 2026. Ford has not (as of 2026) been publicly documented as remotely deleting paid customer features post-sale at scale. Sources: [Ford BlueCruise pricing (Ford Media)](https://media.lincoln.com/content/fordmedia/fna/us/en/news/2024/10/01/ford-lowers-bluecruise-annual--monthly-plan-pricing.html), [Carscoops on BlueCruise pricing](https://www.carscoops.com/2024/10/ford-cuts-bluecruise-pricing-to-50-per-month-or-495-annually/), [NHTSA BlueCruise investigations (Ford Authority)](https://fordauthority.com/2026/04/nhtsa-currently-has-three-ford-bluecruise-investigations-underway/).
value.electrificationStrategy: Ford originally targeted aggressive EV growth but in August 2024 announced a strategic pivot to broaden its lineup with hybrids, EREVs, and smaller affordable EVs alongside BEVs. The Model e division has posted multi-billion-dollar annual losses ($4.8B EBIT loss in 2025) and Ford now expects EV profitability by 2029. By 2030 Ford expects hybrids, EREVs and EVs to be ~50% of global volume (up from 17% in 2025). Future BEV growth concentrated on a new low-cost Universal EV Platform; the first vehicle from it (a midsize pickup) is slated for Louisville Assembly in 2027. The Ford Blue ICE business is being electrified — Ford has stated intent to add a hybrid to every Ford Blue model by 2030. Sources: [Ford broadens electrification strategy (Aug 2024)](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240821550568/en/Ford-Broadens-Electrification-Strategy-to-Reach-More-Customers-Improve-Profitability-Continue-to-Reduce-CO2), [Ford EV strategy shift (2026)](https://greentechlead.com/electric-vehicle/ford-ev-strategy-shift-reshapes-profitability-timeline-cancels-large-models-and-expands-hybrids-52247), [WardsAuto](https://www.wardsauto.com/news/ford-scraps-ev-plans-focusing-hybrids-erevs-new-trucks-battery-storage/808026/).
value.killSwitchPolicy: Ford has not made a public, plain-language commitment on the federal IIJA Section 24220 impaired-driving-detection mandate, but its driver-monitoring posture is the most aggressive of the Detroit Three. BlueCruise already uses a driver-facing camera with infrared illumination to verify driver attention, and a Ford patent application (USPTO, surfaced 2026) describes a vehicle system that tracks facial expressions and emotions and can be tied into vehicle control. The 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act reaffirmed the IIJA Section 24220 mandate. Best read: Ford is positioning to comply via camera-based driver-state monitoring already shipping in BlueCruise vehicles (Mach-E, F-150, F-150 Lightning, Explorer, Expedition) rather than via a separate breath/touch sensor; bypass status is unknown. Sources: [Ford biometric monitoring patent coverage](https://needtoknow.news/2026/04/ford-biometric-monitoring-of-drivers-that-tracks-emotions-that-can-trigger-kill-switch/), [BlueCruise driver monitoring (Ford support)](https://www.ford.com/support/how-tos/ford-technology/driver-assist-features/ford-bluecruise-frequently-asked-questions/), [NHTSA Section 24220 (CarPro)](https://www.carpro.com/blog/nhtsa-section-24220-does-this-scare-you).
value.reliabilityNotes: Mixed signals. Consumer Reports has consistently rated the Mustang Mach-E below-average for predicted reliability since launch (electronics, infotainment, body integrity issues). The F-150 Lightning has had multiple high-profile recalls and an extended production halt (Nov 2024 - 2026, supplier fire + aluminum shortage + profitability), and CR predicted reliability has been below average. By contrast, the Maverick Hybrid and Escape Hybrid have generally rated average or better, leveraging Ford's mature Atkinson-cycle hybrid powertrain shared with prior Fusion/Escape Hybrid generations. J.D. Power 2025 Initial Quality has Ford slightly below industry average. The F-150 PowerBoost hybrid earns positive reviews for capability but has had auxiliary battery and 12V system recalls. Three NHTSA investigations into BlueCruise are open as of April 2026. Sources: [Consumer Reports Mach-E reliability](https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/ford/mustang-mach-e/), [Ford Authority NHTSA BlueCruise probes](https://fordauthority.com/2026/04/nhtsa-currently-has-three-ford-bluecruise-investigations-underway/), [JD Power Ford brand reliability](https://www.jdpower.com/cars/ford).

value.title: Genesis
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Beginning with the 2026 model year, every Genesis EV ships with a factory-installed native NACS port, unlocking the ~20,000-stall Tesla Supercharger network plus the upcoming IONNA joint-venture network (~30,000 stalls planned) ([Genesis Electric](https://www.genesis.com/us/en/genesis-electric), [Genesis Electrified GV70 page](https://www.genesis.com/us/en/electrified-gv70)). 2025 MY Genesis EVs ship with CCS1 and require a NACS-to-CCS adapter for Supercharger access (parent Hyundai Group began distributing free adapters in early 2025). Genesis also offers complimentary Electrify America charging credits on new EV purchases (typically 2-3 years), and integrates ChargePoint and EVgo via Plug & Charge.
value.drmPolicy: Genesis vehicles use Genesis Connected Services (GCS), a 4G LTE telematics platform that requires cellular and GPS coverage to deliver remote start, geofencing, OTA updates, and many in-cabin features ([MyGenesis Connected Services](https://owners.genesis.com/us/en/page/connected-services.html), [Connected Services T&Cs](https://owners.genesis.com/us/en/terms-and-conditions.html)). As of October 2023 GCS is complimentary on 2023+ MY vehicles ([Genesis Newsroom](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/genesis-connected-services-now-complimentary-for-new-owners-of-2023-or-later-model-years-301952498.html)) but the agreement explicitly states Genesis may cancel services if underlying wireless networks change or sunset (3G shutdown precedent: parent Hyundai bricked telematics on older vehicles when AT&T sunset 3G). Core driving functions are not gated on connectivity, but navigation traffic, remote app control, valet alerts, and OTA software updates require an active GCS subscription after the complimentary period. No public documented case of Genesis remotely disabling base driving functions post-sale; Hyundai Group has remotely pushed software updates (e.g., theft-prevention patches for non-Genesis models after the TikTok theft wave) without owner action.
value.electrificationStrategy: Genesis announced in 2021 it would offer only zero-emission (BEV and FCV) models from 2025 launches forward and become 100% zero-emission across its lineup by 2030, with carbon neutrality by 2035 ([Genesis Newsroom](https://newsroom.genesis.com/genesis-presents-vision-for-sustainable-future/), [InsideEVs](https://insideevs.com/news/530339/genesis-outlines-electrification-strategy/)). In April 2026 Genesis softened the all-BEV path, confirming it will introduce advanced hybrids starting in 2026 as a transitional 'efficient entry point into electrification' while keeping BEVs at the top of the lineup ([Genesis Newsroom CEO statement](https://newsroom.genesis.com/genesis-ceo-on-future-of-mobility-we-give-our-customers-what-they-want/)). Hyundai Motor Group has also committed a $26B U.S. investment covering electrification and future tech.
value.killSwitchPolicy: Genesis has not made a public, brand-specific statement on the IIJA Section 24220 'Advanced Impaired Driving Prevention Technology' mandate. Genesis MY25/MY26 vehicles ship with driver attention warning (camera-based fatigue monitoring) but no impairment-based vehicle disablement. There are no public reports of Honda remotely disabling features post-sale or pushing software updates that remove functionality from in-service vehicles. value.chargingNetworkAccess: Karma has not announced partnerships with Tesla Supercharger, Electrify America, EVgo, or ChargePoint. The Revero EREV uses a CCS1 port for DC fast charging; the upcoming Kaveya BEV is also expected to ship with CCS1 at launch. No free-charging promo programs have been announced. Sources: https://karmaautomotive.com/revero/, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karma_Revero
value.drmPolicy: Karma vehicles ship with mandatory connectivity: an embedded telematics system providing OTA software / map updates plus a Karma mobile app for remote door lock/unlock, climate preconditioning, charge scheduling, vehicle-health reporting, and an AR user manual. Karma has publicly announced subscription-style purchases of vehicle features for MY2024+ Reveros via the connected-car app surface built by Audax Labs, but specific feature SKUs and prices have not been disclosed; no public examples of post-sale remote feature reduction. Given the extremely low production volume (160 Reveros globally) and recency of the 3rd-gen platform, there is essentially no third-party / forum reporting on offline operation. Sources: https://audaxlabs.com/connected-car-app/, https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/rightware-kanzi-powers-the-digital-cockpit-and-infotainment-system-in-the-new-karma-revero-592762191.html
value.electrificationStrategy: Karma is an all-electrified luxury brand built on Extended Range Electric Vehicle (EREV) technology, which it positions as the marketplace pioneer of the segment. After originally planning a fully-electric future, Karma pivoted in 2024-2025 to lead with EREV/PHEV models (Revero, Gyesera) due to slower-than-expected EV take-rates in the ultra-luxury segment, with full BEVs (Kaveya) layered in on top. Sources: https://karmaautomotive.com/news/karma-automotives-new-era-dawns/, https://www.greencarreports.com/news/1145678_karma-claims-these-evs-and-phevs-are-coming-in-2025-and-2026
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: Karma has made no public statement on the IIJA-driven federal impaired-driving-detection mandate. As a low-volume (146 vehicles sold in 2024) ultra-luxury maker, Karma will be subject to the same NHTSA rulemaking as every other OEM but has not signaled a hardware vs software approach. Search of Karma press releases, dealer FAQs, and trade press (The Autopian, Green Car Reports) surfaces no commitment either way as of May 2026.
value.reliabilityNotes: Data unavailable: Karma has no Consumer Reports, J.D. Power, or TrueDelta coverage due to volumes well below the reporting thresholds (146 US vehicles sold in 2024). Anecdotal reports on Karma owner forums and Reddit mention long parts lead times and limited dealer service network as the dominant ownership concerns rather than mechanical reliability per se. Sources: https://www.theautopian.com/karma-automotive-sold-just-146-vehicles-last-year-its-ceo-told-me-thats-the-appeal/

value.title: Kia
value.chargingNetworkAccess: **Tesla Supercharger network:** Kia EV6, EV9, and Niro EV owners gained access to 21,500+ Tesla Superchargers in 2025 via the Kia Access app. 2025 MY EV6 and 2026 MY EV9 ship with a factory-integrated NACS port (Plug & Charge supported). 2024-2025 EV6/EV9 with CCS1 ports got free NACS-to-CCS1 adapters if delivered after 2024-09-04; Niro EV and earlier deliveries can buy the adapter for $249 at dealers. **Electrify America:** Kia partners with EA for complimentary charging on EV6 / EV9 / Niro EV — currently 1,000 kWh of free 350-kW DC fast charging over 36 months on new BEV purchases (program details vary by trim/promo). **Other networks:** ChargePoint and EVgo accessible via standard CCS1 (or NACS via adapter), no Kia-specific partnership at the Tesla level. Sources: https://www.kiamedia.com/us/en/media/pressreleases/23210/kia-ev6-ev9-and-niro-owners-gain-access-to-over-21500-tesla-superchargers , https://www.notebookcheck.net/Kia-EV6-and-EV9-get-Plug-Charge-upgrade-with-Tesla-NACS-port-support-for-Superchargers.1125379.0.html , https://insideevs.com/news/768225/kia-ev6-charging-adapter-tesla/
value.drmPolicy: Kia uses the Kia Connect (formerly UVO link) connected-vehicle platform, which is the gating layer for remote start, remote climate, remote lock/unlock, remote seat heat/ventilation, OTA updates, vehicle finder, stolen-vehicle immobilization, Voice Assist, and curfew alerts. New-vehicle purchase or lease includes a complimentary 3-year subscription (all tiers) on 2025 MY; after that, tiered plans are paid (Light free; Connect ~$14.99/mo or $149/yr; Connect+ premium tier ~$24.99/mo). Core driving functions (propulsion, basic A/C, infotainment local features, CarPlay/Android Auto, ADAS) remain functional without an active Connect subscription; only the connected/remote/OTA layer degrades. No public reports of Kia remotely disabling already-shipped features post-sale. Plug & Charge for the 2025 EV6 / 2026 EV9 is delivered through the Kia Access app, which requires a Kia Connect account. Sources: https://owners.kia.com/us/en/about-uvo-link.html , https://owners.kia.com/us/en/uvo-compare-packages.html , https://www.huffineskiacorinth.com/blog/2025/june/8/kia-connect-101-pricing-features-setup-vehicle-compatibility.htm
value.electrificationStrategy: Under its "Plan S" strategy (first announced 2020, expanded at 2024 and 2025 CEO Investor Days), Kia targets global sales of 4.19 million units by 2030, of which 2.33 million (~56%) are to be electrified (1.26M BEV + 1.07M xHEV). In North America, electrified share is targeted at 70% by 2030. Kia plans 15 EV models by 2027 (EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, plus PBVs PV5/PV7/PV9). Sources: https://www.kianewscenter.com/events/all/2023-ceo-investor-day---kia-accelerates-ev-transition-with-target-of-1.6-million-ev-sales-by-2030/s/4432e086-3707-4026-ac57-94855cfc9a6a , https://www.greencarcongress.com/2024/04/20240407-kia.html , https://electriccarsreport.com/2026/04/kia-targets-4-13-million-global-sales-by-2030-with-evs-hybrids-and-pbvs-at-the-core/
value.killSwitchPolicy: Kia has not issued a model-specific public statement on the IIJA Section 24220 impaired-driving-detection mandate (NHTSA NPRM still pending as of 2026-05; industry-wide compliance deadline is currently targeted around 2027 with possible extension). Industry trade group Alliance for Automotive Innovation (of which Kia America is a member) and individually BMW/Ford/GM/Toyota have written NHTSA expressing general support combined with concerns about technology readiness, false-positive rates, and consumer acceptance. Kia's current driver-monitoring stack is Driver Attention Warning (DAW), which is camera-and-steering-input based, software-only, and warns rather than disables. There is no shipping hardware-based BAC or impairment kill-switch on any 2025/2026 MY Kia. Sources: https://www.motor1.com/news/794316/new-cars-mandate-impaired-driver-detection-delay/ , https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/ , https://www.nhtsa.gov/sites/nhtsa.gov/files/2023-07/Report-to-Congress-Advanced-Impaired-Driving-Prevention-Technology_07-17-23.pdf

value.title: Lamborghini
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Lamborghini PHEVs ship with the **CCS1** DC fast-charging port for the US market (inherited from the VW MEB / PPE / Audi platform parts). Unlike Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche, and Scout — which committed to NACS hardware from 2025 and shipped NACS DC adapters for Tesla Supercharger access — Lamborghini, Bentley, and Bugatti were **explicitly excluded** from the Volkswagen Group's NACS announcement. Lamborghini PHEVs (Revuelto 3.8 kWh, Temerario 3.8 kWh estimated, Urus SE 25.9 kWh) all charge primarily via AC (J1772 home / public Level 2); the Urus SE supports DC fast charging via CCS1. No bundled-charging promo (no Electrify America credits, no Supercharger access). Owners typically rely on home Level 2 or public J1772/CCS1 networks (Electrify America, EVgo, ChargePoint) and pay individual session rates. Sources: https://media.vw.com/releases/1891 , https://www.jalopnik.com/volkswagen-audi-porsche-and-scout-finally-commit-to-n-1851113117/ , https://insideevs.com/news/711103/vw-group-ev-nacs-adapter/
value.drmPolicy: Lamborghini uses **Lamborghini Connect** (rebranded from the per-model Urus Connect / Huracán Connect / Revuelto Connect) for telematics, remote vehicle control via the Lamborghini UNICA app, and OTA software updates. Connected services include remote start/lock, vehicle tracking + Security Operations Center alerts on unauthorized entry, track telemetry with on-board camera recording, and Alexa integration that receives OTA updates. Vehicles operate without an active subscription (drive functions are not gated), but app-based remote features, real-time tracking, and OTA telematics updates require connectivity and an active Connect subscription (terms typically bundle a free initial period, then renew at owner's cost — Lamborghini does not publish a public price sheet; renewal is handled through the dealer). No public record of Lamborghini remotely disabling drive features post-sale. The Revuelto's January 2026 NHTSA software recall (rearview camera image not displaying) was remediated via dealer service rather than OTA-fix-only, which suggests safety-critical software paths still require dealer intervention. Sources: https://www.lamborghini.com/en-en/ownership/lamborghini-connect , https://www.lamborghini.com/en-en/ownership/lamborghini-connect/guide-to-connected-services , https://www.lamborghini.com/original/DAM/lamborghini/legal/revuelto/2025/USA_English_Revuelto_disclaimer_website_v1.pdf , https://www.autoblog.com/news/the-lamborghini-revuelto-is-now-on-its-4th-recall
value.electrificationStrategy: Lamborghini's roadmap is called **Direzione Cor Tauri** (Latin for "toward the heart of the Bull"), announced 2021 with the largest investment plan in the company's history. Three phases: (1) celebrate the ICE legacy through 2022; (2) hybridize the entire lineup by end of 2024 (achieved — Revuelto V12 PHEV in 2023, Urus SE V8 PHEV in 2024, Temerario V8 PHEV launched 2024-2025 replacing the Huracán); (3) launch the first fully-electric Lamborghini originally targeted for 2028 (inspired by the Lanzador concept). As of 2026, Lamborghini has pushed the Lanzador EV back and re-positioned it as a hybrid first, with the all-electric Super SUV (Urus successor) targeted for 2029. Goal: 40% reduction in CO2/car vs 2021 levels by 2030. Sources: https://www.lamborghini.com/en-en/news/lamborghini-announces-its-roadmap-for-electrification-direzione-cor-tauri , https://www.carscoops.com/2026/03/lamborghini-ev-delay-hybrids/ , https://robbreport.com/motors/cars/lamborghini-electriciation-roadmap-cor-tauri-1234614005/
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: no public Lamborghini statement located regarding the IIJA-driven federal impaired-driving-detection mandate (HALT/Advanced Impaired Driving Prevention Technology, NHTSA rulemaking targeting ~2027 effective date). As a Volkswagen Group brand, Lamborghini will inherit whatever passive-detection system VW Group standardizes for US-market vehicles. Lamborghini sells only V12 / V8-hybrid PHEV supercars and the Urus SUV (low US-market volumes — ~3,000-3,500 US units/year), so any compliance approach is expected to mirror Audi/Porsche/VW rather than driving its own R&D. Searches across Lamborghini press, owner forums, and trade publications returned no NHTSA filings, no executive statements, and no roadmap commitments on impaired-driving detection. The Revuelto / Temerario / Urus SE all already ship with driver-monitoring-capable hardware (interior cameras for telemetry, steering input sensors, ADAS suite from VW Group) that could in principle be repurposed for passive impairment detection via OTA, but Lamborghini has not announced such use.
value.reliabilityNotes: Lamborghini does not appear in Consumer Reports brand reliability rankings (sample too small — only ~3,000-3,500 US sales/year). J.D. Power lacks a Lamborghini-specific dependability index. TrueDelta similarly has insufficient data. Empirical signal comes from NHTSA recalls: the Revuelto has had **four NHTSA recall campaigns in its first ~30 months** (Oct 2024 windshield wiper connecting rod, Dec 2024 oil-circuit flange screw torque, Jul 2025 door gas-spring pin torque, Jan 2026 rearview-camera software). The October 2024 wiper recall covered 455 vehicles; the July 2025 door recall covered 27 vehicles (20 MY24 + 7 MY25). All are assembly / QC issues plus one software defect, rather than fundamental design faults. The Urus has historically been the volume model and benefits from VW Group platform parts (Q8 / Cayenne / Bentayga sibling) which lifts component reliability vs. an indigenous platform. Lemon-law cases have been filed against the Revuelto. Sources: https://www.cars.com/research/lamborghini-revuelto/recalls/ , https://www.autoblog.com/news/the-lamborghini-revuelto-is-now-on-its-4th-recall , https://californialemonattorneys.com/door-recall-even-a-600k-lamborghini-revuelto-can-be-a-lemon/

value.title: Land Rover
value.chargingNetworkAccess: JLR (Jaguar + Land Rover) announced in 2024 that future Jaguar EVs will adopt the Tesla NACS port and gain Supercharger access; the Range Rover Electric (the brand's first BEV) is widely expected to follow the same NACS path though Range Rover has not issued a separate brand-level press release. Current 2025/2026 Land Rover PHEVs (Range Rover P460e/P550e, Range Rover Sport P460e/P550e, Defender P400e) all use the CCS1 (J1772 Combo) port for DC fast charging at peak rates around 43–50 kW, with public access through Electrify America, EVgo, ChargePoint, and Blink networks. No brand-level free-charging program is bundled with the PHEV lineup in the US; charging credits and roadside assistance are negotiated at the dealer level. Sources: https://insideevs.com/news/688021/jaguar-access-tesla-supercharging-network/ , https://www.motorauthority.com/news/1140893_jaguar-to-adopt-tesla-s-nacs-connector-from-2025 , https://www.rangerover.com/en-us/electric/index.html
value.drmPolicy: Land Rover uses InControl + Pivi Pro connected services. Remote App functionality (remote start/precondition, lock/unlock, vehicle status, geofencing, find-my-car) requires an active InControl Remote subscription; subscriptions come complimentary for an initial period and must be renewed via the in-vehicle Services Store. Per Land Rover's own FAQ: 'If you do not renew InControl Remote or InControl Protect then the associated services will be disabled on your vehicle following the expiry of your subscription.' Core driving and powertrain functions do not require connectivity to operate. SOS Emergency Call (Protect) is also a subscription service. Over-the-air updates are delivered through Pivi Pro and (for newer MY24+ vehicles) the SOTA architecture introduced with the new Range Rover/Range Rover Sport. No widely reported instance of JLR remotely disabling already-purchased hardware features (heated seats, performance) post-sale — unlike BMW's ConnectedDrive seat-heating subscription, JLR has not gated previously standard hardware behind a paywall, though some convenience apps and Wi-Fi data plans are subscription-only. Sources: https://www.landroverusa.com/ownership/infotainment-systems/pivi-faqs.html , https://www.landroverusa.com/ownership/infotainment-systems/subscriptions.html , https://incontrol.landrover.com/jlr-portal-owner-web/static/docs/manuals/owner/MyJaguarLandRoverInControlManual_en_BW.pdf
value.electrificationStrategy: JLR's Reimagine strategy (Feb 2021) committed to all Jaguar and Land Rover nameplates having pure-electric variants by 2030 and JLR achieving net-zero across supply chain, products, and operations by 2039. The first BEV from the Range Rover brand (Range Rover Electric) opened reservations in 2024 and was originally planned for 2025 delivery; deliveries have slipped into 2026. Land Rover Defender BEV is confirmed for ~2027 and a Defender Sport BEV is projected for early 2027. Velar and Range Rover Sport BEVs are anticipated 2026/2027 on the new MLA-derived EMA/Modular Longitudinal Architecture. Until BEVs ship, the lineup is electrified via 48V MHEV (Defender P400 inline-6) and 38.2 kWh PHEV (Range Rover P460e/P550e, Range Rover Sport P460e/P550e, Defender 110 P400e in select global markets). Sources: https://media.jaguarlandrover.com/news/2021/02/reimagine-jaguar-land-rover-strategy-real-change , https://www.landroverusa.com/vehicles/phev/index.html , https://topelectricsuv.com/news/land-rover/land-rover-defender-electric/
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: Land Rover has made no public statement specific to the IIJA Section 24220 advanced impaired-driving prevention mandate. JLR does include camera-based Driver Condition Monitor (drowsiness/inattention warning) as part of the standard ADAS stack on new Range Rover and Range Rover Sport, which is the foundational hardware NHTSA is expected to leverage in any final rule, but JLR has not announced whether implementation will be hardware-based (passive cabin alcohol/BAC sensing) or software-based (camera + steering input pattern analysis), and has not commented on bypass behavior. NHTSA itself has stated no technology yet meets the accuracy threshold the rule will require; the rulemaking timeline has slipped beyond the original 2024 target with implementation expected ~2027 at the earliest. Sources: https://www.motor1.com/news/794316/new-cars-mandate-impaired-driver-detection-delay/ , https://madd.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Advanced-Impaired-Driving-Prevention-Technology-Fact-Sheet-December-2023-1.pdf
value.parentCorporation: JLR (Jaguar Land Rover), owned by Tata Motors
value.reliabilityNotes: Land Rover consistently ranks at or near the bottom of US reliability surveys. Consumer Reports's 2024 Brand Reliability rankings placed Land Rover 22nd of 22 brands surveyed (lowest), with a predicted reliability score of 14/100; JD Power's 2024 Vehicle Dependability Study (3-year-old vehicles) had Land Rover at 215 problems per 100 vehicles, substantially worse than the industry average of ~190. Range Rover and Range Rover Sport historically suffer high incidence of air-suspension faults, electrical/InControl gremlins, and infotainment glitches; Defender (L663) is newer and has shown more electronic-architecture teething issues than mechanical ones. The new MLA-Flex platform under the L460 Range Rover and L461 Range Rover Sport remains relatively unproven; TrueDelta long-term tracking shows above-average frequency of unscheduled service visits in the first ownership year. Sources: https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/car-reliability-owner-satisfaction/who-makes-the-most-reliable-cars-a7824554938/ , https://www.jdpower.com/cars/ratings/dependability , https://www.truedelta.com/Land-Rover

Lexus announced in 2023 it would adopt NACS (Tesla connector) for future BEVs starting 2025; current RZ 450e uses CCS1. Adapter availability and Supercharger access through Toyota/Lexus charging programs is rolling out. Lexus Drive Connect (cloud navigation, voice assistant, intelligent assistant) and Remote Connect (remote start, lock/unlock via app) operate on trial-to-paid subscriptions. Lexus has been criticized for moving previously-included features behind paywalls (e.g., remote start). Most core driving and safety functions operate without connectivity, but cloud navigation and OTA updates require it. Sources: https://www.lexus.com/connected-services , https://pressroom.lexus.com/lexus-app/ , https://www.thedrive.com/news/lexus-connected-services-paywall
value.electrificationStrategy: Lexus has announced a goal to sell only battery-electric vehicles in North America, Europe, and China by 2030, and globally by 2035. The brand is part of Toyota Group, which has historically favored hybrid technology over BEVs. Sources: https://pressroom.lexus.com/lexus-on-the-road-to-electrification/ , https://www.toyota.com/usa/electrification/ , https://global.toyota/en/newsroom/corporate/38818143.html

value.title: Lincoln
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Lincoln EV/PHEV owners have access to Tesla's Supercharger network (15,000+ stalls) starting spring 2024 via a Ford-supplied CCS-to-NACS adapter, plus the BlueOval Charge Network aggregating Electrify America, EVgo, ChargePoint, and others (~120,000 chargers). Future Lincoln EVs starting MY2025 were announced to ship with the native NACS port, but with no Lincoln BEV currently in market, this has not materialized — the Corsair PHEV uses J1772 for Level 2 only (no DC fast charging). Sources: https://www.northtownelincoln.com/blog/2024/march/20/lincoln-customers-can-now-charge-on-tesla-are-you-ready-to-make-the-switch.htm , https://www.tesla.com/NACS
value.drmPolicy: Lincoln vehicles rely on FordPass Connect / Lincoln Connected Services for OTA updates, remote start, vehicle status, and the Lincoln Way app. The driver-assist suite BlueCruise requires an active Connected Service plan — newer vehicles come with a complimentary 4-year subscription, after which renewal is required to keep hands-free highway driving functional. There is no public documentation of Ford/Lincoln remotely disabling already-paid features post-sale (in contrast to, e.g., Tesla / BMW heated seats). Cars operate without internet for core driving but lose connected features (remote start, OTA, BlueCruise) without subscription. Sources: https://www.lincoln.com/technology/connected-services/ , https://www.lincoln.com/support/how-tos/lincoln-technology/driver-assist-features/lincoln-bluecruise-frequently-asked-questions/
value.electrificationStrategy: Lincoln initially announced plans to deliver three new fully electric vehicles by mid-decade and add a fourth by the end of 2026, including electric versions of the Corsair, Nautilus, Aviator, and Navigator. This plan has been substantially scaled back. Parent Ford CEO Jim Farley has stated Ford/Lincoln will pivot away from an all-electric lineup in favor of hybrid and EREV (extended-range electric vehicle) powertrains, with BEVs concentrated on the affordable end. As of MY2026, Lincoln has no BEV in the US market and only two electrified offerings: the Corsair Grand Touring PHEV and the Nautilus Hybrid (full hybrid). The Aviator Grand Touring PHEV was discontinued after MY2023. Sources: https://www.motorauthority.com/news/1135061_lincoln-reportedly-plans-up-to-five-evs-through-2026-including-electric-navigator , https://carbuzz.com/lincolns-no-ev-policy-might-be-smart/ , https://www.chargedfleet.com/10168361/lincoln-plans-to-produce-four-ev-models-by-2026
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: No specific public Lincoln/Ford statement located regarding the IIJA Section 24220 impaired-driving-detection mandate. Lincoln already ships a driver-facing infrared camera as part of BlueCruise that tracks eye gaze and head position for drowsy/distracted detection, which provides a hardware foundation for compliance with whatever final NHTSA rule emerges. As of May 2026, NHTSA has not finalized the rule (original Nov 2024 deadline missed); the rule has been delayed because no commercially available passive BAC detection technology has been validated. Implementation in production vehicles is unlikely before late 2027. Sources: https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/ , https://www.carscoops.com/2026/03/nhtsa-impaired-driving-detection-tech/
value.reliabilityNotes: Consumer Reports has historically rated Lincoln below the industry average. The 2024-2025 Nautilus redesign (Ford CX430 platform, China-built) introduced significant new infotainment hardware (48-inch panoramic display) that has drawn early reliability concerns; the Corsair remains on a long-running platform shared with the Ford Escape. J.D. Power 2024 Initial Quality awards rated Lincoln Nautilus as 'Highest Ranked' in its segment but the brand overall scores mid-pack. value.title: Lotus
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Eletre and Emeya ship with **CCS1** charging ports in the US (800V architecture, peak 350-367 kW DC fast charging). Lotus has announced future NACS adoption with adapters for early CCS1 owners, but no firm launch date or rollout schedule has been published as of May 2026. The Lotus Charging program partners with **ChargePoint** to provide route-planning and access to a network of ~77,000 charging stations across North America. No formal Tesla Supercharger partnership exists; third-party NACS-to-CCS1 adapters work at compatible V3/V4 Superchargers via the Tesla app. No continuing free-charging promotion has been documented for US Eletre/Emeya buyers. Sources: [Lotus Charging](https://www.lotuscars.com/en-US/lotus-charging), [EV Charge+ Eletre guide](https://evchargeplus.com/ev-specification/lotus-eletre/).
value.drmPolicy: Lotus vehicles (Eletre, Emeya) ship with the **Lotus Connect** connected-services suite and **Hyper OS** infotainment, both reliant on cellular/5G data connectivity. Core connectivity (vehicle status, remote climate/charging, OTA updates) is bundled with the vehicle for a service period; enhanced features are offered via the optional **Lotus Connect Prestige** paid subscription tier (additional comfort, control and security functions, plus enhanced infotainment). The cars perform regular over-the-air software updates (OTAU). No documented cases of Lotus remotely disabling features post-sale have surfaced in owner forums or press as of May 2026. However, the dependency on Lotus's cloud and the Geely/Lotus Technology backend (China-hosted infrastructure for some services) is a known concern in owner communities. Lotus has not published a clear statement on minimum offline functionality. Sources: [Lotus Connect](https://www.lotuscars.com/en-GB/lotus-connect), [Lotus HyperOS](https://www.lotuscars.com/en-IT/hyper-os), [The Lotus Forums - Prestige subscription](https://forums.thelotusforums.com/topic/124763-lotus-prestige-ends-on-november-30th/).
value.electrificationStrategy: Lotus announced its **Vision80** strategy in 2018, committing to become a fully all-electric luxury brand by 2028 (its 80th anniversary). Under Geely ownership (majority stake since 2017), Lotus launched a BEV-only lineup for new mainstream models — the Eletre SUV (2023), Emeya GT sedan (2024), and Evija hypercar. However, in early 2025 Lotus Technology CEO Qingfeng Feng publicly retreated from the all-electric-only timeline, announcing a pivot to hybrid and ICE supercars due to 'a complex market environment'. The Emira sports car (ICE, Toyota-sourced V6/I4) remains in production; a Type 135 hybrid hypercar is targeted for 2028. Lotus has stated it will pivot fully to BEV 'when market conditions are ripe'. Sources: [Electrive](https://www.electrive.com/2021/04/29/geely-subsidiary-lotus-to-become-dedicated-ev-brand/), [Yicai Global](https://www.yicaiglobal.com/news/geelys-ultra-luxury-carmarket-lotus-drops-full-electrification-plans-ceo-says), [eletric-vehicles.com](https://eletric-vehicles.com/lotus/lotus-drops-all-electric-strategy-pivots-to-hybrid-and-ice-supercars/).
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: no public statement from Lotus Cars or Lotus Technology Inc. addressing the IIJA-mandated impaired-driving-detection (Section 24220) requirement as of May 2026. Searched manufacturer press releases, NHTSA rulemaking comments, and US auto-industry trade press; Lotus has not publicly commented on its compliance approach. As a low-volume luxury manufacturer (sub-10,000 US units/year), Lotus would still be subject to FMVSS rules once finalized. Given the Eletre/Emeya already ship with a driver-monitoring camera (DMS) for Highway Assist and a 5G-connected ADAS sensor stack (34 sensors, 12 cameras, 4 LiDAR, NVIDIA Drive Orin), the hardware foundation for a software-based system likely exists.
value.reliabilityNotes: Lotus is a niche, low-volume manufacturer; Consumer Reports and J.D. Power do not publish reliability rankings for the brand due to insufficient sample size. Early Eletre owner reports on TheLotusForums and LotusTalk highlight: (1) a faulty 12V super-capacitor causing 12V battery drain and requiring roadside jump starts; (2) accelerated 12V/HV battery drain in cold weather; (3) cosmetic build-quality complaints (wheel stone-chipping, plastic trim, stitching). No NHTSA recalls have been issued for the US-market Eletre or Emeya as of May 2026. Older Lotus models (Evora, Elise/Exige) had a history of transmission, electrical, and oil-cooler-hose issues, but these are not directly applicable to the EV models. Brand reliability data is sparse; buyers should expect a luxury-startup risk profile. Sources: [Lotus Eletre problems - LotusTalk](https://www.lotustalk.com/threads/lotus-eletre-problems.549582/), [Eletre Quality/Reliability thread - LotusTalk](https://www.lotustalk.com/threads/eletre-quality-reliability-and-lotus-customer-service.547718/), [J.D. Power 2025 Eletre page](https://www.jdpower.com/cars/2025/lotus/eletre).

value.title: Lucid
value.chargingNetworkAccess:
All Lucid Air owners (2022+ model years) gained access to the Tesla Supercharger network on July 31, 2025 via a Lucid-supplied DC NACS-to-CCS1 adapter ($220). Charging on Superchargers is capped at ~50 kW. The newly launched 2026 Air still uses a native CCS1 port; the upcoming Gravity SUV is the first Lucid with a native NACS port (per Lucid's NACS adoption announcement). Lucid customers also get access to Electrify America (older promos provided 3 years of free charging at launch; current promos vary by trim/quarter) and the ChargePoint/EVgo networks via standard CCS1.

Sources:

- https://lucidmotors.com/stories/lucid-adopt-nacs
- https://ir.lucidmotors.com/news-releases/news-release-details/all-lucid-airs-gain-access-23500-tesla-superchargers-2026-lucid/
value.drmPolicy:
Lucid vehicles are deeply connected: the Lucid mobile app is described by Lucid as 'a core part of Lucid ownership' and is used for remote climate, charging, locking, and Supercharger payment initiation. Connectivity is currently included; Lucid has publicly stated it will eventually charge for connectivity (DreamConnect Premium has been mentioned by sales reps as Gravity-specific at launch). OTA updates push new features and bug fixes regularly (e.g., DreamDrive enhancements, Apple CarPlay arrived via OTA). No public reports of Lucid remotely disabling owned vehicles' core driving function post-sale; the principal connectivity-dependent features are app remote control, navigation routing, voice assistant, and Supercharger payment.

value.electrificationStrategy:
Lucid is a pure-play BEV manufacturer; every vehicle it sells (Air, Gravity) is battery-electric, with no ICE/HEV/PHEV products planned. The company positions its in-house high-voltage architecture (900V on Air, 926V on Gravity) and class-leading efficiency (~5 mi/kWh on Air Pure) as the strategy. A midsize platform launched on Gravity (Nov 2024) is the basis of a forthcoming midsize SUV/sedan (~$50k target) expected late 2026.

Owners report the powertrain, range, and ride quality as exceptional, with most complaints centered on the infotainment/UX and early build-quality items (panel fit).
