value.title: Maserati
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Folgore BEVs ship with a CCS1 port in North America. On 2026-03-19, Stellantis (parent of Maserati) opened Tesla Supercharger access to all current Stellantis BEVs including the GranTurismo Folgore, GranCabrio Folgore, and Grecale Folgore via a Stellantis-approved NACS-to-CCS1 adapter sold through Mopar.com and Stellantis BEV-certified dealers (~$230) ([Stellantis press release 2026-03-19](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/stellantis-expands-north-america-fast-charging-access-as-dodge-jeep-ram-fiat-and-maserati-bevs-plug-in-to-the-tesla-supercharger-network-302718753.html), [Electrek 2026-03-19](https://electrek.co/2026/03/19/the-last-domino-falls-stellantis-evs-now-have-tesla-supercharger-access/)). Adapter is required; native NACS will not arrive on Stellantis vehicles until the 2027 Dodge Charger Daytona. Beyond Supercharger, Maserati operates the Maserati Public Charge app (Free2move Charge backend) that aggregates Electrify America, EVgo, ChargePoint, and other major CCS1 networks ([Maserati North America charging](https://www.maserati.com/us/en/models/folgore/north-america)). No included-free-charging promotion is currently offered in North America.
value.drmPolicy: Maserati vehicles use the Maserati Connect telematics platform (5G-enabled on Folgore models) with an Ubigi-provided cellular data plan ([Maserati Connect](https://www.maserati.com/us/en/ownership/maserati-connect), [Ubigi for Maserati](https://maserati.ubigi.com/assistance/)). Core driving functions do not require active connectivity, but a meaningful chunk of the value proposition is subscription-gated: remote lock/unlock, remote climate, vehicle status, geofencing, stolen-vehicle assistance, and over-the-air map/software updates all live in the Maserati Connect app and require an active subscription after the included trial period (typically several years on Folgore, then a paid renewal in the low hundreds of dollars per year) ([Maserati Connect Customer Guide PDF](https://www.maserati.com/content/dam/maserati/international/catalogues/gb/Maserati_Connect_Customer_Guide_EN.pdf)). No public reporting documents Maserati remotely disabling a previously-delivered feature post-sale; the brand is too low-volume to have generated the BMW-heated-seats-style controversy. Data unavailable: no specific public confirmation that the car is fully drivable indefinitely with the Connect SIM disabled, beyond the general telematics-industry norm that core propulsion and ADAS run locally.
value.electrificationStrategy: Maserati originally committed to a fully electric lineup by 2030 under the "Folgore" (Italian for "lightning") sub-brand as part of Stellantis' Dare Forward 2030 plan, with every new model launching electric-first ([Maserati / Stellantis Media](https://www.media.stellantis.com/us-en/maserati/press/maserati-confirms-commitment-to-100-engineered-and-made-in-italy-strategic-plan-focused-on-bold-electrification-and-sustainable-growth), [Electrek 2024-01-25](https://electrek.co/2024/01/25/maserati-reiterates-all-electric-made-in-italy-strategy-in-wake-of-delays-rifts-with-local-govt/)). The plan has since been substantially walked back. In 2025, Stellantis cancelled the MC20 Folgore in favor of an updated gas MCPura ([TFLcar 2025-03](https://tflcar.com/2025/03/maserati-mc20-folgore-canceled-news/)) and delayed the next-gen Quattroporte Folgore from 2025 to 2028 ([Motor Authority](https://www.motorauthority.com/news/1142045_redesigned-maserati-quattroporte-with-electric-power-delayed)). Stellantis subsequently wrote off roughly EUR 1.5 billion of Maserati electrification investment ([MoparInsiders](https://moparinsiders.com/stellantis-scraps-maseratis-electrification-plans/)). As of MY2026 the US Folgore lineup is three BEVs (GranTurismo, GranCabrio, Grecale); the 2030 all-electric target is no longer an active public commitment.
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: Maserati and Stellantis have not made a public, brand-specific statement on the IIJA Section 24220 impaired-driving-detection mandate (expected MY2027) as of 2026-05. The broader regulatory picture is that NHTSA missed its 2024 rulemaking deadline, received an extension, and the final standard is still being negotiated ([KBB](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/), [The Autopian](https://www.theautopian.com/new-cars-sold-in-america-will-be-actively-watching-and-judging-you-and-may-decide-to-not-let-you-drive/)). Stellantis brands (including Maserati) currently rely on the existing camera-based driver-attention monitoring shipped on Folgore models for related driver-state functions; no Stellantis brand has announced a dedicated hardware impaired-driving interlock. Expect any future implementation to be camera/behavior based and OTA-deliverable through the Maserati Intelligent Assistant stack.
value.reliabilityNotes: Maserati has long had a reputation for below-average reliability and high cost of ownership. Consumer Reports projects the 2025 Grecale to be less reliable than the average new vehicle, citing Maserati's brand history ([Consumer Reports 2025 Grecale Reliability](https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/maserati/grecale/2025/reliability/)). J.D. Power Vehicle Dependability ranks Maserati near the bottom of the luxury segment in most recent studies. The Folgore lineup is too new and too low-volume to have a meaningful reliability dataset (Folgore deliveries began in 2024 for GranTurismo, 2024-25 for Grecale and GranCabrio). Notably, Maserati's extended-warranty programs explicitly exclude battery electric vehicles, which limits owners' financial protection beyond the 4yr/50k bumper-to-bumper ([Scottsdale Maserati](https://www.scottsdalemaserati.com/manufacturer-information/maserati-warranty/), [ConsumerAffairs Maserati Extended Warranty](https://www.consumeraffairs.com/automotive/maserati-extended-warranty.html)).

value.title: Mazda
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Mazda announced NACS adoption in January 2024 for North American BEVs launching from 2025 onward, giving Mazda BEV customers access to 15,000+ Tesla Superchargers. Notably, Mazda has not committed to a CCS1-to-NACS adapter program for its existing US BEV (the discontinued MX-30); the NACS port will arrive natively on the next Mazda BEV in 2027. Current Mazda PHEVs (CX-90 PHEV, CX-70 PHEV) are AC-only (Level 1/Level 2, J1772) and have no DC fast-charge port at all. No partnerships with Electrify America, EVgo, or ChargePoint are bundled at point-of-sale. Sources: https://news.mazdausa.com/2024-01-15-Mazda-Adopts-North-American-Charging-Standard-NACS-for-North-American-BEVs, https://electrek.co/2024/01/16/mazda-nacs-adoption-tesla-superchargers/
value.drmPolicy: Mazda has a notable history of restrictive connectivity and DRM behavior. In 2021 Mazda quietly removed remote start from the physical key fob, requiring use of the MyMazda app (Mazda Connected Services). After a 3-year complimentary trial, ongoing remote start/lock/unlock/vehicle-status access requires a paid subscription (~$10/month as of 2024). In October 2023 Mazda sent a DMCA takedown to an open-source developer (Brandon Rothwell) who built a Home Assistant integration that talked to Mazda servers without the official app, citing DMCA Section 1201 anti-circumvention. The vehicle itself still operates fully offline for driving functions; the DRM concern is on convenience/remote features and aftermarket integrations. Sources: https://www.thedrive.com/news/mazda-quietly-ditched-key-fob-remote-start-for-subscription-app, https://www.carscoops.com/2024/09/mazdas-remote-start-subscription-draws-ire-of-noted-right-to-repair-advocate/, https://consumerrights.wiki/w/Mazda_remote-start_subscription
value.electrificationStrategy: Mazda's 2030 'Multi-Solution Strategy' (announced March 2025) keeps a mixed lineup of ICE, hybrids, PHEVs, and BEVs through 2030, with BEVs projected at 25-40% of global sales by 2030. The first dedicated Mazda BEV on a new platform launches in 2027 with battery cells from Panasonic Energy. Mazda will have 7-8 BEV models globally by 2030 and is leveraging a 'Lean Asset Strategy' and partnerships with Toyota (software/electrical architecture, ~90% Toyota-based) and Changan (China BEVs) to cut planned investment from 2 trillion yen to 1.5 trillion yen. Sources: https://newsroom.mazda.com/en/publicity/release/2025/202503/250318a.html, https://news.mazdausa.com/2025-03-18-Mazda-Accelerates-Toward-an-Electrified-Future-with-Strategic-Innovations, https://insideevs.com/news/623055/mazda-full-scale-launch-bevs-2028-2030/
value.killSwitchPolicy: Mazda has not made a specific public statement on its product-level plan for the federal IIJA Section 24220 impaired-driving-detection mandate. Mazda has shown a 'Co-Pilot' concept (Co-Pilot 1.0 launched on the larger Mazda6/CX-60 platforms in Japan in 2022, Co-Pilot 2.0 planned later) that uses in-cabin driver-monitoring cameras to detect incapacitation/loss of consciousness, autonomously decelerate, pull to the shoulder, and call emergency services. This is camera-based driver-monitoring (DMS) rather than alcohol-sensing; current US Mazda models do not include any factory impaired-driving lockout. NHTSA's final rule under IIJA Section 24220 is delayed to no later than November 2027, so the earliest production-vehicle integration would likely be MY2029+. Sources: https://www.theautopian.com/new-cars-sold-in-america-will-be-actively-watching-and-judging-you-and-may-decide-to-not-let-you-drive/, https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/

Consumer Reports' 2024-2025 brand reliability survey ranked Mazda 6th overall and 3rd among brands to buy used. However, the newer Large Platform vehicles (CX-90, CX-70) have generated multiple software-related recalls in 2024-2025 covering stalling, PCM/ECM faults, PHEV inverter software, surround-view camera, 360-view monitor, defroster, and false-positive automatic braking. Owners charge at home via L2 or use any standard J1772 public AC charger. The W1 hypercar similarly relies on AC home/garage charging. No free-charging promotions exist. Source: https://cars.mclaren.com/us_en/artura
value.drmPolicy: McLaren vehicles use the IRIS infotainment platform with optional 'McLaren Pure Connect' connected services (vehicle tracking, geofencing, valet mode, service reminders, stolen-vehicle protection). The Track Telemetry app is a paid-option software unlock through IRIS rather than a recurring subscription; the optional Video Data Logger (VDL) adds hardware cameras. No public evidence of post-sale remote feature reduction or pay-to-unlock heated-seat-style schemes. As ultra-low-volume exotics, McLarens depend on dealer service tools for many calibration tasks, which is a de facto connectivity dependence even though the car itself runs offline. No published remote-bricking incidents. Sources: https://cars.mclaren.com/gl_en/ownership/mclaren-track-telemetry ; https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ikontechnologies.mclarenpure.connect
value.electrificationStrategy: McLaren has explicitly rejected a near-term pure BEV strategy. CEO Nick Collins stated in 2025 that McLaren will only introduce an EV 'when the market requires it' and that 'real supercars' with electric power will not arrive until around 2030. Current strategy centers on V8 PHEV supercars (using a new Ricardo-developed V8 paired with a small ~10 kWh battery from Nio under a 2024 technology partnership) and the limited-production W1 PHEV hypercar. A V8 hybrid four-door SUV (codename P47) is planned for 2028 under the new CYVN ownership. All models launching in 2030 are expected to remain combustion-based with hybrid assistance. Sources: https://www.motor1.com/news/690229/mclaren-boss-supercar-not-electric-2030/ ; https://www.autoblog.com/news/mclaren-says-no-to-evs-as-it-prepares-new-hypercars-and-an-suv ; https://eletric-vehicles.com/mclaren/mclaren-ceo-says-no-plans-for-ev-model-a-year-after-gaining-access-to-nios-tech/
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: McLaren has made no public statement regarding compliance with the IIJA Section 24220 advanced impaired-driving prevention technology mandate. value.title: Mercedes-Benz
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Mercedes-Benz BEV drivers gained access to the Tesla Supercharger network (20,000+ stalls in US/Canada) starting February 2025 via the Mercedes me Charge service with Plug & Charge functionality. For existing CCS1-equipped Mercedes EVs (all current EQS/EQE/EQB), Mercedes sells a branded NACS-to-CCS1 DC adapter at authorized dealerships for $185 (released Q1 2025). Mercedes is also building its own Mercedes-Benz High-Power Charging (HPC) network in North America in partnership with MN8 Energy, targeting 400+ hubs / 2,500+ stalls with up to 400 kW. New Mercedes EVs from late 2025/early 2026 will begin shipping with native NACS ports (CLA with EQ Technology is the first). Mercedes me Charge also aggregates Electrify America, EVgo, ChargePoint, and others into a single billing relationship. Sources: https://media.mbusa.com/releases/mercedes-benz-bev-drivers-gain-access-to-tesla-supercharger-network-from-february-2025 ; https://www.mbusa.com/en/charge/nacs-charging
value.drmPolicy: Mercedes-Benz EVs require connectivity to the Mercedes me cloud for full functionality (live navigation, OTA updates, charging-network integration via Mercedes me Charge, Plug & Charge with Tesla Supercharger network). The cars will start and drive without a cellular connection, but many infotainment and connected services become unavailable. **Subscription-locked features documented**: Mercedes-Benz introduced an 'Acceleration Increase' subscription for EQ400-series cars (EQE 350, EQS 450) in late 2022 priced at $1,200/year (or $60/mo) that electronically uncorks ~24% more horsepower and torque (boost of ~80hp and torque, cutting 0-60 by 0.8-1.0 seconds). The hardware is identical between the lower and upper power tiers — the difference is purely software. Mercedes also offers other connected subscription services via Mercedes me Connect with various tiers. To date, Mercedes has not been publicly reported to have remotely reduced features owners previously had, but the Acceleration Increase precedent establishes the model. Sources: https://www.techdirt.com/2022/11/28/mercedes-puts-faster-acceleration-behind-a-subscription-paywall/ ; https://www.inverse.com/gear/mercedes-benz-ev-eq-acceleration-annual-subscription-price ; https://www.endurancewarranty.com/learning-center/make-model/what-is-mercedes-benz-acceleration-subscription-fee/
value.electrificationStrategy: Mercedes-Benz originally committed in 2021 to going all-electric by 2030 'where market conditions allow' with a €40 billion electrification investment. In February 2024, CEO Ola Källenius walked back this target at the company's annual meeting, now projecting that electrified vehicles (BEV + PHEV + HEV combined) will reach ~50% of sales by 2030 rather than 100% BEV. Mercedes will continue ICE production well into the 2030s. New EV platform strategy: MMA (entry/compact, launched in 2025 with the redesigned CLA with EQ Technology) and MB.EA (mid/large luxury, launching with the GLC EQ in May 2026 and the C-Class EQ later in 2026). Sources: https://electrek.co/2024/02/22/mercedes-backtracks-ev-plans-gas-cars-2030s/ ; https://www.motorauthority.com/news/1142387_mercedes-benz-backtracks-on-plan-to-go-full-electric-by-2030 ; https://www.mbusa.com/en/future-vehicles
value.killSwitchPolicy: Mercedes-Benz has not made detailed public statements about its specific implementation plan for the IIJA-mandated impaired-driving-detection system (NHTSA expected to finalize the rule around 2026-2027). As one of the German big-three (Mercedes, BMW, Audi), Mercedes participates in industry coalitions (Alliance for Automotive Innovation) that have lobbied NHTSA for flexibility on the rule's technical requirements. Mercedes already ships DRIVER ATTENTION ASSIST (drowsiness detection via steering inputs) as standard on essentially every US model; future implementations are likely to extend this camera/sensor stack with impairment-detection logic. No publicly disclosed hardware kill-switch architecture exists as of 2026-05. Data unavailable: specific bypassability or hardware-vs-software architecture for Mercedes's planned IIJA implementation — Mercedes has not published technical details and no investigative reporting has surfaced the specifics.
value.reliabilityNotes: Consumer Reports projects below-average reliability for the 2025 Mercedes-Benz brand overall and specifically rates the EQS and EQE below average for predicted reliability, citing software and electronics (infotainment glitches, driver-assist faults, warning-light recurrences) as the primary trouble areas rather than the battery or drive motors. J.D. Power's Initial Quality Study and Vehicle Dependability Study place Mercedes-Benz below the industry average for problems per 100 vehicles. The 2025 EQE has been subject to 3 NHTSA recalls and the 2025 EQS SUV 2 recalls as of early 2026. Owner reviews on Edmunds and KBB for 2024-2025 EQS/EQE average ~3.5-4.0 out of 5 for reliability, with repeat dealership visits being the most common complaint. value.title: Mini
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Current US-market MINI Electric vehicles (Cooper SE J01 hardtop, Countryman SE ALL4 U25) use CCS1 ports. As of December 10, 2025, BMW Group enabled Tesla Supercharger access for eligible BMW EVs, but the BMW USA announcement (https://www.bmwusa.com/all-electric/tesla-nacs-charging.html) does not list MINI vehicles — only the BMW i4, i5, i7, and iX received the required Remote Software Upgrade. MINI access to Tesla Superchargers has been previewed publicly (Shell Recharge / MINI App integration with Tesla's network was announced for 2025) but is not confirmed live for the J01 or U25 platforms as of May 2026. The MINI App integrates Electrify America, Shell Recharge, ChargePoint, EVgo, and Blink. Native NACS ports are not expected on MINI until a future Neue Klasse-derived platform. No free DC-fast-charge promo is currently bundled with new MINI EV purchases in the US. Sources: https://www.bmwusa.com/all-electric/tesla-nacs-charging.html ; https://www.bimmerfile.com/2025/12/20/bmw-evs-can-now-use-tesla-superchargers-supported-models-adapters-and-how-it-works/ ; https://www.miniusa.com/model/electric-vehicles.html
value.drmPolicy: MINI uses the parent BMW Group connected-services stack. The 2025+ MINI Operating System 9 (Android Open Source Project based) includes 'MINI Connected Base' (always included; eCall, TeleService, basic Remote Services) and 'MINI Connected Plus' (optional monthly/annual subscription via My MINI Garage, the MINI App, or the in-car MINI Connected Store) for premium digital services. MINI USA publicly stated in April 2025 it has no plans to expand U.S. subscription-based software offerings beyond Connected Plus and the existing Remote Engine Start subscription. Remote start (after the included trial) and Connected Plus features are subscription-locked. The car operates and drives without an active subscription or cellular signal — only connected/remote-services features go dark. BMW Group has never been publicly reported as remotely disabling a working feature post-sale on a sold vehicle (unlike BMW Germany's brief 2022 heated-seat-subscription trial, which it walked back globally in 2023 before MINI ever implemented it on the US market). Sources: https://www.motoringfile.com/2025/04/30/miniusa-says-no-thanks-to-expanding-software-subscriptions-for-now/ ; https://www.miniusa.com/why-mini/mini-connected-technology.html ; https://faq.miniusa.com/s/article/FAQ-Will-my-my-2025-MINI-Cooper-2-Door-receive-regular-Remote-Software-Upgrades-HDW5g?language=en_US
value.electrificationStrategy: MINI committed in March 2021 to becoming an all-electric brand by 2030, with the last ICE-engined MINI model originally targeted to launch in 2025. By 2027, the brand stated it expected half of its global sales to be EVs. The plan has since been slightly relaxed: BMW's 'power of choice' approach now extends through the 5th-generation family debuting in early 2030, with the global all-electric transition targeted for ~2031. The new J01 Cooper Electric (built in Zhangjiagang, China, with Spotlight Automotive — a joint venture with Great Wall Motor) and the U25 Countryman Electric (built in Leipzig, Germany) launched the current EV-only family. Future BEVs (e.g., Aceman EV — not US-bound) will sit on the Neue Klasse-derived platform. value.killSwitchPolicy: No MINI-specific public statement on Section 24220 of the IIJA (the federal Advanced Impaired Driving Prevention Technology mandate). NHTSA missed its 2024 deadline to issue the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard, has been granted extensions, and as of April 2026 no final rule has been published. BMW Group (MINI's parent) ships a Driver Attention Camera in MINI Operating System 9 vehicles as part of the standard ADAS suite, which provides drowsiness/distraction warnings but is not a kill switch — it cannot prevent the car from operating. No hardware Driver Monitoring System interlock has been announced for any 2025 or 2026 MINI. Whatever standard NHTSA finalizes, MINI will be required to comply on the federal effective date (currently expected late 2026 or in 2027). value.title: Mitsubishi
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Mitsubishi's only currently-sold electrified vehicle in the US is the Outlander PHEV, which uses **CHAdeMO** for DC fast charging (a legacy connector with shrinking network support) and **SAE J1772** for AC charging. Top trims (SEL / SEL Black Edition / Platinum) are equipped with the DC fast-charge port; lower trims are AC-only. No partnership with Tesla Supercharger network announced — Mitsubishi is the only major automaker that has not announced NACS adoption as of 2026-05-21, attributed in trade coverage to its lack of a current BEV. ChargePoint, EVgo, and Electrify America CCS1 networks are not directly accessible to the Outlander PHEV without third-party CHAdeMO adapters. The forthcoming 2026 BEV (Nissan LEAF-based) will likely adopt NACS following Nissan's announced transition, but no official Mitsubishi confirmation yet. Sources: [GreenCarReports NACS roundup](https://www.greencarreports.com/news/1140904_evs-from-these-brands-will-soon-use-the-tesla-nacs-charge-port), [Outlander PHEV charging guide](https://www.mitsubishicars.com/cars-and-suvs/outlander-phev/performance).
value.drmPolicy: Mitsubishi vehicles use the **MITSUBISHI CONNECT** telematics platform with two service packages: Safeguard (in-vehicle, includes SOS, automatic collision notification, stolen vehicle assistance) and Remote Services (smartphone app for remote start, lock/unlock, climate, charging schedule for PHEV). Two years included on new vehicles, then annual subscription. Core driving functions do **not** require an active subscription; vehicle operates fully offline. PHEV charging schedule and remote climate features require connectivity. From MY2025 Outlander forward, Mitsubishi added **Stolen Vehicle Assistance with Engine Blockage** — a remote ignition-blocking capability invoked by law enforcement after a verified police-report case number; once the engine is turned off it cannot be restarted until Mitsubishi's call center re-enables it. This is the only known remote disable capability in the fleet and is gated behind a verified police case, not unilateral OEM action. No public reporting of post-sale feature reduction or paywall migration to date. Sources: [MITSUBISHI CONNECT product page](https://www.mitsubishicars.com/mitsubishi-connect), [Stolen Vehicle Assistance manual](https://www.mitsubishi-connect.com/en/SafeguardRemote/Manual/outlander_Quick_US/contents/).
value.electrificationStrategy: Under the **Momentum 2030** North American five-year plan, Mitsubishi commits to launching one new or refreshed model annually through 2030, with the lineup spanning ICE, MHEV, HEV, PHEV, and BEV. Global parent targets electrified vehicles at 50% of sales by 2030 and 100% by 2035, with a 40% reduction in vehicle CO2 by 2030. A new BEV co-developed with Alliance partner Nissan (based on the next-generation Nissan LEAF) is scheduled to arrive at US dealers in summer 2026; as of 2026-05-21 it is announced but not yet on sale, with naming, specs, and pricing TBA. Sources: [Mitsubishi press: Momentum 2030](https://media.mitsubishicars.com/en-US/releases/release-a8c162bbdb31ace11a0c57edd4000f49-mitsubishi-motors-announces-momentum-2030-north-american-five-year-business-plan), [Mitsubishi press: New BEV summer 2026](https://media.mitsubishicars.com/en-US/releases/mitsubishi-motors-confirms-all-new-battery-electric-vehicle-will-be-sold-in-north-america-starting-summer-2026), [Electrek coverage](https://electrek.co/2026/03/02/new-ev-based-on-nissan-leaf-launching-this-summer/).

As of 2026-05-21, NHTSA has missed its statutory rulemaking deadline and no final rule is in force; the industry as a whole is in a holding pattern. Mitsubishi already ships the Driver Attention Alert system (a fatigue/inattention warning) on most Outlander trims, but this is advisory only and not a kill-switch implementation. Searches across press releases, owner forums, and trade press surfaced no Mitsubishi-specific IIJA position paper or hardware/software plan. Sources: [NHTSA kill switch deadline coverage (KBB)](https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/).

Mitsubishi historically scores mid-pack in Consumer Reports brand reliability rankings (typically top 10), benefiting from a relatively conservative product cadence. J.D. Power Initial Quality and Dependability rankings place Mitsubishi in the mid-pack for mainstream brands. The Outlander PHEV powertrain itself (4th-gen sold since 2022) has been broadly trouble-free per owner forums, with the camera/infotainment software being the dominant complaint cluster. value.chargingNetworkAccess: Polestar signed an NACS agreement with Tesla in 2023. As of 2025 model year and forward, new Polestar vehicles sold in North America ship with the NACS port natively (Polestar 3, Polestar 4); pre-2025 CCS1 vehicles (Polestar 2) gained Tesla Supercharger access via a $230 Polestar-branded NACS adapter and OTA software update starting late 2024. Vehicles also continue to support CCS1 fast-charging via included/optional adapter. No Polestar-specific bundled-free-charging promotion is publicly active in 2026, though Plug & Charge is supported at compatible CCS networks (Electrify America). Sources: https://www.engadget.com/transportation/evs/north-american-polestar-owners-can-now-use-the-tesla-supercharger-network-164046134.html, https://www.greencarreports.com/news/1144867_polestar-and-volvo-gain-tesla-supercharger-access-nacs-adapters-cost-230
value.drmPolicy: Polestar vehicles are heavily software-defined and rely on cellular connectivity for the full feature set (Google built-in services, Google Maps with real-time energy routing, Google Assistant, OTA updates, Polestar Connect app for remote control, charging status, preconditioning). Core driving works offline, but navigation, voice assistant, remote app control, charging-network roaming, and connected services degrade when the cellular link or Google account session is unavailable. OTA updates are free and delivered over cellular; the Performance Software Upgrade (e.g. ~$1,200 for Polestar 2 Dual Motor adding ~68 hp) is sold online as a paid software unlock — a clear precedent of horsepower gated behind a one-time DRM purchase rather than a hardware change. No public examples of post-sale remote feature removal/downgrade for paying owners have surfaced, but the OTA architecture means the manufacturer retains technical capability to alter feature behavior remotely. Sources: https://www.polestar.com/us/owning-a-polestar/ota/, https://www.polestar.com/us/support/faq/over-the-air-updates/, https://www.currentnotesev.com/p/thoughts-on-polestar-2-software-update
value.electrificationStrategy: Polestar is a pure-electric performance brand. Originally a Volvo racing/performance partner (Flash Engineering, founded 1996; rebranded Polestar Racing; acquired by Volvo in 2015), it was spun out in October 2017 as a standalone all-electric brand jointly owned by Volvo Cars and Geely Holding. Its entire current and announced lineup (Polestar 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7) is battery-electric — there are no PHEV, HEV, MHEV, or ICE products. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polestar, https://www.polestar.com/us/
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: No Polestar-specific public statement found on its implementation plan for the IIJA-mandated advanced impaired driving prevention technology (NHTSA rulemaking, ~2027 target). Polestar already ships driver-monitoring cameras (Smart Eye driver-monitoring system in the Polestar 3 and Polestar 4) as part of its standard ADAS suite, which positions the platform for a software-implemented passive-monitoring approach if/when the federal rule lands, but no confirmed roadmap has been published. value.chargingNetworkAccess:
Porsche Charging Service gives owners access to ~700,000 public charging points in the US (via Electrify America, EVgo, ChargePoint, and other roaming partners) through a single Porsche ID and the My Porsche app. Taycan and Macan Electric owners get 3 years of complimentary 30-minute Electrify America DC fast charging sessions (one per visit, with a cooldown). Porsche announced in 2023 that Taycan and Macan Electric will gain NACS port access via adapter starting 2025 and native NACS ports on next-gen architecture (~2026+). Porsche is also building 'Porsche Charging Lounge' destination chargers in Europe and a planned US rollout. Home charging via the included Porsche Mobile Charger Connect (J1772).

value.drmPolicy:
Porsche operates Porsche Connect, a connected-services platform that ties many in-car features to a manufacturer cloud account. The base Connect package is included for 3 years on new vehicles; renewals are paid subscriptions. Porsche generated controversy by gating features like adaptive cruise on later 2023+ Macans/Taycans (and certain options on Cayenne) behind a 'function on demand' (FoD) software-upgrade model — buyers can pay to unlock pre-installed hardware features (e.g., active lane keeping, Power Steering Plus on some models, intelligent range manager) post-purchase. Porsche has not been publicly documented remotely disabling already-purchased features post-sale, but the FoD architecture creates that capability. Porsche Communication Management (PCM) infotainment requires an active SIM/eSIM for live navigation, charging-network search, and remote app functions; the car drives offline but loses charging-network routing, live traffic, Spotify/Apple Music streaming, and remote climate/charge control.

value.electrificationStrategy:
Porsche originally targeted 80% of new vehicle sales being all-electric by 2030, but in mid-2024 the company walked back this firm target, citing slower-than-expected EV adoption. CEO Oliver Blume in 2024-2025 stated Porsche will keep building combustion and hybrid models 'well into the 2030s' and that the brand will adapt to demand. The 718 Boxster/Cayman successors are still planned as BEVs (delayed to ~2027). The next-gen Cayenne arrives in 2026 as a BEV alongside the existing PHEV/ICE Cayenne (sold in parallel). 911 stays ICE/hybrid only for now (T-Hybrid 2025+).

Any 2027 NHTSA rule would require a software/hardware retrofit to the existing driver-monitoring stack. value.title: Ram
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Stellantis announced NACS adoption in 2024 for North American EVs but has not specified whether Ram models will ship with a native NACS port or rely on a CCS1-to-NACS adapter, and whether existing BEV/PHEV models will be retrofitted. The 2026 Ram 1500 Ramcharger ships with a CCS1 port and accepts up to 175 kW DC fast charging. Ram has not announced a charging-network partnership equivalent to Ford BlueOval Charge Network or GM Energy. Owners can access public networks (Electrify America, EVgo, ChargePoint) on a pay-per-use or membership basis. Free-charging promotions tied to vehicle purchase are not currently advertised. Sources: https://www.destinationcharged.com/news/stellantis-adopts-nacs-to-expand-fast-charging-availability-in-2026/ , https://insideevs.com/news/751663/ramcharger-ev-and-ice-mpg/
value.drmPolicy: Ram vehicles use Stellantis Uconnect 5 infotainment with Connected Services. Some features are subscription-gated through Uconnect Services (~$14.99/month) and Connect Wi-Fi PLUS — these include remote start from the smartphone app, remote door lock/unlock, real-time traffic, navigation map updates (Navigation Package subscription), Dynamic Range Mapping, and SiriusXM. Key-fob remote start works without subscription. Stellantis in 2021 attempted to expand its subscription model and there was consumer backlash against potential retroactive feature-gating; the company appears to have walked back some of those plans. A 10-year Safety & Security Package (automatic SOS, theft alert, roadside assistance) is included with vehicle purchase. No published evidence of Stellantis remotely disabling already-purchased features in Ram trucks post-sale. The vehicle's core driving functions (engine, transmission, brakes, steering) do not require active connectivity. Sources: https://www.driveuconnect.com/faq.html , https://media.stellantisnorthamerica.com/newsrelease.do?id=25241&mid= , https://pickuptrucktalk.com/2021/12/stellantis-subscription-service-includes-remote-start-too/
value.electrificationStrategy: Ram has had a turbulent electrification arc. The brand originally announced an all-electric Ram 1500 REV (BEV) and a range-extended Ram 1500 Ramcharger (EREV) as its two-pronged electrified pickup strategy under Stellantis Dare Forward 2030. The all-electric Ram 1500 REV BEV was canceled in September 2025 due to slowing demand for full-size BEV pickups in North America. The Ramcharger EREV was repeatedly delayed (originally targeting 2024, then 2025, then early 2026) and was renamed the Ram 1500 REV after the BEV cancellation. As of May 2026, the Ramcharger has begun reaching select US dealers as a 2026 model. The Ram 1500 also offers a 48V mild-hybrid (eTorque) on its V6 Pentastar and (returning for 2026) 5.7L HEMI V8, plus a 48V mild-hybrid system on the new 3.0L Hurricane I6. Stellantis has publicly stated electrification pace should be governed by demand rather than command, indicating a slower transition than its earlier all-EV-by-2030 ambitions. Sources: https://insideevs.com/news/772186/ram-1500-rev-dead/ , https://www.wardsauto.com/news/archive-auto-stellantis-cancels-ram-1500-bev-electric-pickup-rev-extended-range/760779/ , https://www.media.stellantis.com/em-en/ram/press/range-extended-ram-1500-ramcharger-to-lead-brand-s-electrification-push
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: Stellantis has made no public statement specific to Ram regarding its implementation plan for the IIJA-mandated impaired-driving-detection technology (FMVSS rule expected late 2026 / 2027). The federal rule is itself still being drafted by NHTSA — NHTSA missed its 2024 statutory deadline and has admitted no commercially-available passive detection technology meets the accuracy requirements. Likely implementation across all major makers (including Ram) will be camera-based in-cabin driver monitoring already present in current Uconnect-equipped Ram trucks (driver attention monitoring is part of current ADAS suites). Search of Stellantis/Ram press releases through May 2026 found no Ram-specific statement on hardware vs software architecture, bypass options, or owner override. Sources: https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/ , https://www.motor1.com/news/794316/new-cars-mandate-impaired-driver-detection-delay/
value.reliabilityNotes: Ram 1500 historically rated below segment average on Consumer Reports predicted reliability — the brand has had issues with electrical/infotainment systems, transmission shift quality, and recall frequency. J.D. Power Initial Quality Study has placed Ram at or near top of its segment in some recent years (segment-leading IQS 2022) but long-term dependability lags. The new 3.0L Hurricane I6 introduced for 2025 is too new for reliability data; the 5.7L HEMI V8 returning for 2026 has decades of field data and is generally regarded as durable but with known concerns (lifter/cam, MDS). The Ramcharger EREV is a new architecture (first model year 2026) with no field data. Sources: https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/ram/1500/ , https://www.jdpower.com/cars/ram

value.title: Rivian
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Rivian operates the Rivian Adventure Network (its own DC fast-charging network for owners) and provides Supercharger access via a Rivian-approved NACS-to-CCS1 DC adapter on Gen-2 2025 vehicles (the adapter ships standard with new 2025 R1T/R1S in the US and Canada). Model Year 2026 R1T/R1S and the new R2 ship with native NACS (SAE J3400) charge ports and charge directly at the Tesla Supercharger network without an adapter. Rivian vehicles also work on Electrify America, EVgo, ChargePoint, and other CCS networks (with the Gen-2 NACS-only 2026 cars using a CCS-to-NACS adapter for legacy CCS sites). No continuing free-charging promo as of 2026-05; past promos have included credits at the Rivian Adventure Network for specific deliveries. value.drmPolicy: Rivian vehicles are highly connected and most non-driving features depend on Rivian's cloud services. A two-tier Connect model exists: Connect (standard, included) provides OTA updates, live navigation, remote app commands, Phone-as-a-Key, Alexa Basic, and tethering; Connect+ ($14.99/month or $149.99/year) adds in-vehicle Wi-Fi hotspot, satellite imagery, streaming-app data, Alexa connected commands, Gear Guard Live Cam, Google Cast, and YouTube. Subscription lapse removes the Connect+ features but the car continues to drive. Owners can fully disable connectivity, but doing so also disables navigation, lane-keeping assist, and OTA updates per Rivian's own support docs. Rivian publishes a domestic-violence revocation flow that strips a former user's Phone-as-a-Key and app access — a documented case where Rivian remotely modifies who may interact with a specific vehicle. No public examples of Rivian remotely disabling a paid feature on a sold vehicle. value.title: Subaru
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Subaru committed in November 2023 to adopt the Tesla NACS (SAE J3400) connector on North American BEVs starting in 2025 [https://media.subaru.com/pressrelease/2115/1/subaru-adopt-tesla-north-american-charging-standard-north]. The 2026 Solterra, Trailseeker, and Uncharted ship natively with NACS ports. 2023-2025 Solterra owners use a Subaru-supplied NACS adapter for Tesla Supercharger access, activated via the SubaruConnect app starting October 2025 [https://media.subaru.com/newsrelease.do?id=2384]. Access to 25,000+ Tesla Supercharger stalls is now available to Solterra owners. Subaru does not have a branded charging network; relies on the open public network (Electrify America, EVgo, ChargePoint) plus Tesla Superchargers. No headline free-charging promotion currently active for new Solterra purchases as of mid-2026.
value.drmPolicy: Subaru vehicles use the STARLINK connected services system (cellular telematics built into the car). Core driving functions do not require connectivity — vehicles operate fully offline. However, several conveniences are subscription-gated through SUBARUCONNECT/STARLINK packages: Safety Plus (SOS/automatic collision notification), Security Plus (remote start, remote door lock/unlock, stolen-vehicle recovery, boundary/speed/curfew alerts), and Concierge. Free trial periods at purchase, then paid renewal. Tesla Supercharger access for 2023-2025 Solterra owners is gated through the SubaruConnect app [https://media.subaru.com/newsrelease.do?id=2384], which is a connectivity-dependent feature. No documented history of Subaru remotely disabling previously delivered features post-sale. Subaru does not publicly publish OTA software-update policy for non-Solterra models; the Solterra (Toyota-platform-based) does receive OTA updates from the Toyota infrastructure. Subaru does not currently subscription-gate physical hardware features such as heated seats. Sources: [https://www.subaru.com/subaru-starlink/starlink-safety-and-security.html] [https://www.subaruxvforum.com/threads/disabling-starlink.186712/].
value.electrificationStrategy: Subaru has revised its electrification roadmap multiple times. In 2023, Subaru announced a target of 50% BEV share of global sales by 2030 (~600,000 BEVs annually) [https://insideevs.com/news/679960/subaru-accelerates-electrification-50-bev-share-2030/]. In November 2025, citing slowing EV demand and rising hybrid demand, Subaru pulled back: only ~40% of global sales to be HEV+BEV combined by 2030, with most of its 1.5 trillion yen electrification spend redirected toward hybrids and a delay of full-scale BEV mass-production investment [https://www.electrive.com/2025/11/12/subaru-deprioritises-electric-models-and-increases-focus-on-hybrids/] [https://www.autoblog.com/news/how-subaru-is-reshaping-its-ev-roadmap-in-response-to-slowing-demand]. In-house BEV production planned at the Yajima plant starting ~2025 (mixed production); a dedicated BEV line at Oizumi is targeted for ~2027. Long-term: 90% vehicle emissions reduction by 2050. Currently Subaru offers two HEVs (Forester Hybrid, Crosstrek Hybrid) and three BEVs (Solterra, Trailseeker, Uncharted) in the US for MY2025/2026; BEVs are jointly developed with Toyota (Solterra/bZ4X, Trailseeker/bZ Woodland, Uncharted/C-HR platform).
value.killSwitchPolicy: Data unavailable: Subaru has made no public statement regarding implementation of the IIJA-mandated impaired-driving-detection system (Section 24220, expected around 2027). The current EyeSight Driver Assist suite includes DriverFocus (a camera-based distraction/drowsiness monitor) on higher trims that warns the driver but does not disable the vehicle. No public roadmap from Subaru on hardware vs. software approach for the federal mandate as of research date (2026-05-21).

value.reliabilityNotes: Subaru as a brand traditionally ranks mid-pack in J.D. Power Vehicle Dependability and Consumer Reports brand reliability. value.title: Tesla
value.chargingNetworkAccess: Tesla owns and operates the Supercharger network — the largest, most reliable DC fast-charging network in North America (>2,500 US stations, >25,000 stalls as of 2025). The Supercharger network uses Tesla's proprietary NACS (North American Charging Standard) connector, which the rest of the industry is in the process of adopting (Ford, GM, Rivian, Hyundai, Kia, Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Honda, Toyota, Volvo, Polestar, Lucid, Nissan, Subaru, Acura, Genesis, JLR, VW, Audi, Porsche have all signed on, mostly with native NACS ports starting MY2025-2026). Tesla vehicles have native NACS and access the full Supercharger network at full speed. Tesla also enables CCS1 stations via an adapter (sold separately) — Electrify America, EVgo, ChargePoint, and ChargeFinder all interoperate via CCS1 adapter, though most non-Tesla stations are slower than Superchargers. New-vehicle free-Supercharging promos have been intermittent and trim-specific (historically: free unlimited for early Model S/X; periodic short-duration free Supercharging promos for new Model 3/Y/X/S). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Charging_Standard , https://www.tesla.com/NACS , https://www.batterytechonline.com/charging/these-11-ev-makers-charging-networks-will-use-tesla-nacs-connector
value.drmPolicy: Tesla has the auto industry's most extensive and aggressive software-DRM regime. (1) Acceleration Boost: a software-only unlock costing ~$2,000 that adds ~0.5s to 0-60 with no hardware change — pure DRM gate. (2) Full Self-Driving (Supervised): as of Feb 2026 sold exclusively as a $99/month subscription (was a one-time $8,000-$15,000 purchase historically) — Tesla discontinued the perpetual-license option. (3) Premium Connectivity ($9.99/mo or $99/yr) gates live traffic data, satellite-view maps, in-car streaming media, Caraoke, and web browser over cellular; without it, you only get Wi-Fi-zone access to those features. (4) Heated rear seats and heated steering wheel were historically software-locked on cars that already had the hardware — Tesla charged owners to unlock features the hardware already supported. (5) Battery capacity software-limiting: early Model S/X with 60kWh designation had a 75kWh pack software-capped, with unlock-on-purchase offered. (6) Remote feature revocation: Tesla has documented history of disabling Supercharging and removing 'free unlimited Supercharging' from cars when ownership transfers occur or when cars pass through Tesla auctions, even if previously advertised — see https://electrek.co/2020/02/12/tesla-disables-supercharging-salvaged-vehicles/ and https://teslamotorsclub.com/tmc/threads/lost-supercharging-on-car-bought-from-3rd-party-dealer.228406/ . (7) Salvage-title vehicles have Supercharging permanently disabled by Tesla regardless of owner repair quality. (8) OTA updates are mandatory in practice — features can be added or removed without owner consent. Sources: https://www.notateslaapp.com/tesla-reference/1040/tesla-acceleration-boost-a-complete-guide , https://insideevs.com/news/784386/tesla-fsd-subscription-only-2026/ , https://www.notateslaapp.com/tesla-reference/551/what-is-tesla-premium-connectivity-what-is-included-and-what-is-not-how-much-does-it-cost , https://insideevs.com/news/399152/tesla-disable-fast-charging-salvage/
value.electrificationStrategy: Tesla is a BEV-only automaker — every passenger vehicle it sells is battery-electric, and the company has no announced plans to produce ICE, HEV, PHEV, or MHEV vehicles. Founded explicitly to accelerate the world's transition to sustainable energy. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. , https://www.britannica.com/money/Tesla-Motors
value.killSwitchPolicy: Tesla has not made an explicit public statement about NHTSA's IIJA Section 24220 impaired-driving-detection mandate (expected to take effect late 2026 / early 2027). However, Tesla is uniquely positioned among automakers because all current Teslas (Model 3 refresh and later, Model Y refresh and later, Model S/X 2021+, Cybertruck) already have a forward-facing cabin camera above the rearview mirror that Tesla actively uses for vision-based driver attention monitoring during Autopilot and FSD (Supervised). This is the exact hardware category the federal mandate is expected to require. Tesla's existing system: monitors gaze direction, head position, and eye state; issues 'strikes' when the driver looks away; suspends Autopilot for one week after 5 strikes; processes images on-device per Tesla's privacy statements (not transmitted to Tesla servers absent opt-in or a safety event). The system is hardware-bound and cannot be bypassed — covering the camera with tape disables Autopilot. There is no kill switch or remote-stop function tied to impairment detection today; the system only restricts driver-assist features, not basic propulsion. Tesla has not announced whether or how this will be extended to comply with the federal impaired-driving mandate. Sources: https://temai.tech/blogs/temai-blogs/the-truth-about-the-tesla-interior-camera , https://www.teslarati.com/tesla-dms-camera-denial-death/ , https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/
value.reliabilityNotes: Tesla reliability has improved substantially but remains polarized. 2025 Consumer Reports: Tesla rose to 9th out of 26 brands (up from 17th the prior year). The Model 3 and Model Y now get 'average' predicted reliability — both are CR-recommended. The Model S and Model X consistently rank below average. The Cybertruck has been below average due to extensive recalls. 2025 J.D. Power Vehicle Dependability Study: Tesla scored 209 PP100 (problems per 100 vehicles, 3-year-old vehicles), still below the 190 industry average, ranking near the bottom of mainstream brands but improving year-over-year. Persistent issue categories: panel gaps and paint quality (improved with Austin/Shanghai production); software bugs (touchscreen freezes, phantom warnings); 12V battery failures; door handle and window-regulator failures on older cars; minor trim/fit issues; service-network capacity (long wait times, mobile service availability varies by region). Cybertruck specifically: 8+ recalls in first 18 months including the April 2024 accelerator-pedal-pad recall (could stick floor-flat) and the March 2025 cant-rail trim delamination recall covering all 46,096 Cybertrucks built. value.chargingNetworkAccess: All Volvo BEVs ship with a CCS1 charging port through MY2025 and a built-in NACS port on most MY2026 cars (including the refreshed EX90). MY2025 EX90 buyers got a free NACS adapter; older Volvo EV owners can buy the adapter at retail. Volvo Cars enabled Tesla Supercharger access starting November 18, 2024, granting compatible Volvo EVs DC-fast access to ~29,000 Tesla Superchargers nationwide; Supercharger locations show up in the in-car Google Maps and the Volvo Cars app. Volvo also has roaming on Electrify America, EVgo, ChargePoint, and the broader Plug & Charge network. Free-charging promos have rotated over the years (early EX90 buyers got 500 kWh of Electrify America credit) but are not currently a headline incentive. Sources: https://www.volvocars.com/us/l/north-american-charging-standard/, https://www.wardsauto.com/news/archive-auto-volvo-cars-releases-nacs-adapter-tesla-supercharger-ev-charging/731924/, https://www.volvocarsmobile.com/supercharger-network-access-nacs.htm
value.drmPolicy: Volvo's modern cars (EX/EC, current XC/V/S) run Volvo Car UX on Android Automotive OS with Google Built-in (Google Maps, Google Assistant, Play Store). Owners get four years of complimentary Google connectivity at purchase; after that Google services require the owner to renew via Volvo's subscription. Core driving functions do not require connectivity, but Google Maps navigation, voice assistant, app updates, remote app features (lock/unlock, climate preconditioning, charge scheduling), and any OTA software updates all require cellular or Wi-Fi connectivity. Volvo has used OTA to deliver new functionality (Pilot Assist downloadable upgrade for $499–$595 on 2021–2025 cars with Google Built-in) and to fix major shipping defects, most notably the EX90's software backlog from 2024–2025. There is no public record of Volvo remotely disabling features post-sale as punishment, but Volvo retains the technical capability via the connected platform. Sources: https://www.volvocars.com/us/support/topic/56b126a04cecae0fc0a8015133ca61ef/, https://www.wardsauto.com/news/volvo-biggest-ota-update-software-comapny-history-google-maps-android-automotive-os/813588/, https://www.swedespeed.com/threads/pilot-assist-now-available-as-a-downloadable-software-upgrade-for-499.695699/
value.electrificationStrategy: Volvo's plan once aimed at 100 percent electric by 2030. In September 2024 Volvo Cars walked that back, saying it now expects 90 to 100 percent of global sales by 2030 to be electrified — meaning BEV or PHEV — with up to 10 percent allowed to be MHEV. As of MY2026 every Volvo sold in the US is electrified: BEV (EX30, EX40, EC40, EX90), PHEV (XC60 T8, XC90 T8), or 48V mild-hybrid (XC60 B5/B6, XC90 B5/B6, V60 Cross Country B5, XC40 B4/B5). Sedans (S60, S90) have been discontinued in the US after MY2025. Sources: https://www.volvocars.com/intl/news/our-company/electrification-update-2024/, https://electriccarsreport.com/2025/10/volvo-car-usa-announces-major-upgrades-and-new-models-as-part-of-its-electric-2026-lineup/, https://shopkunes.com/blog/what-volvos-are-discontinuing-in-2026
value.killSwitchPolicy: Volvo is in front of the federal impaired-driving-detection mandate, not behind it. The EX90 ships with a standard interior sensing system that uses cabin cameras and capacitive steering-wheel sensing to detect drowsiness, distraction, and impairment, and can escalate from gentle nudge to persistent alert to (per Volvo's stated capability) safely stopping the car on the shoulder with hazards on. Volvo publicly positions this as their answer to the IIJA driver-impairment-detection requirement. The system is software/hardware combined (driver-monitoring camera plus capacitive wheel) and is not user-disableable on the EX90. Volvo also offers a 'Care Key' that owners can hand to a young or borrowed driver and which speed-limits the car. There is no public Volvo statement about bypassability; the system is integrated into Volvo Car UX. Sources: https://www.automotive-fleet.com/10182151/volvo-driver-sensing-system-aims-to-reduce-distracted-drowsy-driving-crashes, https://ev.com/news/volvo-ex90s-driver-understanding-system-named-one-of-times-best-inventions-of-2024, https://www.media.volvocars.com/global/en-gb/media/pressreleases/304020/your-volvo-car-will-understand-you-when-youre-not-at-your-best-and-step-in-when-you-need-support
value.reliabilityNotes: Consumer Reports' 2024 brand reliability rankings put Volvo near the bottom of luxury brands (ranked 24 of 30 in 2024 and similarly low in 2023), driven heavily by infotainment, software, and electrical issues. J.D. Power's 2024 Vehicle Dependability Study (3-year-old cars) ranked Volvo 30 of 31, with 218 problems per 100 vehicles vs. industry average of 190 PP100. The EX90's well-documented 2024–2025 software backlog (missing features at launch, multiple OTA waves to deliver promised CarPlay, ADAS, bidirectional charging) is a continuation rather than reversal of that pattern. PHEV models (XC60 T8, XC90 T8) have a better field reputation than the EX90 but still trail German and Japanese luxury averages. Sources: https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/car-reliability-owner-satisfaction/who-makes-the-most-reliable-cars-a7824554938/, https://www.jdpower.com/business/press-releases/2024-us-vehicle-dependability-study, https://insideevs.com/news/781786/volvo-aaos-update-delay/
